fn check_references(tx: &Tx<'_>, next: &Schema,sources:&BTreeMap<String,Table>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    for (name, table) in next.tables.iter().filter(|(_, t)| t.ephemeral.is_none()) {
        let t = tx.num(name)?;
        let mut bad = super::adopt_refusals::Samples::default();
        let mut statement=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT DISTINCT d.id,d.column_name,d.parent_id,d.invalid FROM _dormant_refs d LEFT JOIN r p ON p.t=d.parent_t AND p.id=d.parent_id WHERE d.t=?1 AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM r child WHERE child.t=d.t AND child.id=d.id) AND (d.invalid=1 OR (p.id IS NULL AND d.invalid!=2)) ORDER BY d.id,d.column_name")?;
        let mut rows = statement.query([t])?;
        while let Some(row) = rows.next()? {
            let column: String = row.get(1)?;
            let id:String=row.get(0)?;
            if table.columns.contains_key(&column) && !super::authority_origin::obsolete_ref(tx,t,&id,&column,table,sources.get(name))? {
                bad.add(
                    &row.get::<_, String>(0)?,
                    &format!(
                        "{column} → parent {} (deleted/reused/missing)",
                        row.get::<_, String>(2)?
                    ),
                );
            }
        }
        if bad.count > 0 {
            return Err(refuse(format!(
                "table {name}: {}; dormant references cannot acquire another parent lifetime; keep the current release and repair the named references, or prune the dormant storage before restoring",
                bad.describe()
            )));
        }
        if let Some(through) = &table.through {
            {
                let mut bad = super::adopt_refusals::Samples::default();
                super::activation_walk::walk_metered(tx,t,crate::rows::adoption::Work::DECODE,None,|id,row,meter| {
                    let restored: bool = tx.conn().query_row(
                        "SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_refs WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2)",
                        params![t, id],
                        |r| r.get(0),
                    )?;
                    if !restored {
                        return Ok(());
                    }
                    // The captured deadline belongs to one parent lifetime,
                    // even if an older schema allowed retargeting the active ref.
                    let parent_t = tx.num(&through.parent)?;
                    let current = row
                        .field(&through.reference)
                        .ok()
                        .and_then(|v| v.as_str().ok());
                    let mut evidence=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT parent_t,parent_id,(SELECT name FROM _catalog WHERE num=parent_t) FROM _dormant_refs WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2 AND column_name=?3")?;
                    for edge in evidence.query_map(
                        params![t, id, crate::schema::through::PARENT_DEADLINE],
                        |r| {
                            Ok((
                                r.get::<_, i64>(0)?,
                                r.get::<_, String>(1)?,
                                r.get::<_, String>(2)?,
                            ))
                        },
                    )? {
                        let (old_table, old_id, old_name) = edge?;
                        if old_table != parent_t || current != Some(old_id.as_str()) {
                            bad.add(
                                id,
                                &format!(
                                    "{}.{}: recorded {} [{}], current {} [{}]",
                                    name,
                                    through.reference,
                                    old_name,
                                    old_id,
                                    through.parent,
                                    current.unwrap_or("<missing>")
                                ),
                            );
                            return Ok(());
                        }
                    }
                    if let Ok(Value::Id(parent_id)) = row.field(&through.reference) {
                        if through.live.is_some() || crate::rows::Rows::restored_live_authority(tx,name,id)? {
                            let bytes:Option<i64>=tx.conn().query_row("SELECT octet_length(data) FROM r WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2",params![parent_t,parent_id],|r|r.get(0)).optional()?;
                            meter.heap((bytes.unwrap_or(0) as u64).saturating_mul(64).saturating_add(4096))?;
                        }
                        if let Some(parent) = tx.get(&through.parent, parent_id)? {
                            let parent =
                                crate::schema::row_image(&parent, &next.tables[&through.parent]);
                            // @ref LLP 3000.014.000#71-dormant-restoration-identities-are-a-relation — live policy restamps current inputs after preserving parent lifetime.
                            if through.live.is_none() && !crate::rows::Rows::restored_live_authority(tx,name,id)? && through.fields.iter().any(|(capture, field)| {
                                row.field(capture)
                                    .ok()
                                    .is_some_and(|value| Some(value) != parent.field(field).ok())
                            }) {
                                bad.add(id,&format!("{}.{} parent {parent_id}: captured audience/identity changed",name,through.reference));
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    Ok(())
                })?;
                if bad.count > 0 {
                    return Err(refuse(format!(
                        "table {name}: {}; restore cannot rebind historical audience/deadline captures; restore the original parent reference and audience under the current release, then `snapback4 rollback <dir> --to N`, or explicitly `snapback4 prune <dir> --allow-destructive`",
                        bad.describe()
                    )));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub(super) fn delete(tx: &Tx<'_>, t: i64, id: &str, name: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    super::backfills::delete(tx,t,id)?;
    if !enabled(tx)? {
        return Ok(());
    }
    tx.conn().execute(
        "UPDATE _dormant_refs SET invalid=1 WHERE parent_t=?1 AND parent_id=?2 AND invalid=0",
        params![t, id],
    )?;
    let narrowed=super::narrowed::present(tx.conn())?;
    let home=if narrowed {" OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_narrow_rows WHERE t=?4 AND id=?2)"} else {""};
    tx.conn().execute(&format!("UPDATE _assets SET released_at=COALESCE(released_at,?3) WHERE home_table=?1 AND home_id=?2 AND (home_column IN (SELECT column_name FROM _dormant_values WHERE t=?4 AND id=?2){home})"),params![name,id,crate::now_ms(),t])?;
    tx.conn().execute(
        "DELETE FROM _dormant_values WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2",
        params![t, id],
    )?;
    tx.conn().execute(
        "DELETE FROM _dormant_rows WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2",
        params![t, id],
    )?;
    if narrowed {tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _dormant_narrow_rows WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2",params![t,id])?;}
    tx.conn().execute(
        "DELETE FROM _dormant_refs WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2",
        params![t, id],
    )?;
    Ok(())
}

pub(super) fn holds_home(tx: &Tx<'_>, table: &str, column: &str) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
    if !enabled(tx)? {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    let narrowed=if super::narrowed::present(tx.conn())? {" OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_narrow_rows n JOIN _catalog c ON n.t=c.num WHERE c.name=?1)"}else{""};
    Ok(tx.conn().query_row(&format!("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_tables WHERE table_name=?1) OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_columns WHERE table_name=?1 AND column_name=?2){narrowed}"),params![table,column],|r|r.get(0))?)
}

/// Fetch only destination cells on live transitions, after paying their full
/// serialized/decoded coexistence in the owning activation page/row account.
pub(super) fn restored_values(tx:&Tx<'_>,t:i64,id:&str,table:&Table,meter:&mut crate::meter::Meter)->Result<Vec<(String,String)>,RuntimeError> {
    if !super::live_activation::active(tx)? {
        return Ok(tx.conn().prepare_cached("SELECT column_name,data FROM _dormant_values WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2")?.query_map(params![t,id],|r|Ok((r.get(0)?,r.get(1)?)))?.collect::<Result<_,_>>()?);
    }
    t: i64,
    id: &str,
    column: &str,
    kind: &ColumnType,
    value: &Value,
) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    tx.conn().execute(
        "DELETE FROM _dormant_refs WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2 AND column_name=?3",
        params![t, id, column],
    )?;
    let mut refs = Vec::new();
    references(kind, value, &mut refs);
    for (parent, parent_id) in refs {
        add_reference(tx, t, id, column, &parent, &parent_id)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn add_reference(
    tx: &Tx<'_>,
    t: i64,
    id: &str,
    column: &str,
    parent: &str,
    parent_id: &str,
) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    let parent_t = tx.num(parent)?;
    let invalid = !tx.conn().query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM r WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2)",params![parent_t,parent_id],|r|r.get::<_,bool>(0))?
        && !tx.conn().query_row(
            "SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_rows WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2) OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_narrow_rows WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2)",
            params![parent_t, parent_id],
            |r| r.get::<_, bool>(0),
        )?;
    tx.conn().execute(
        "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO _dormant_refs VALUES(?1,?2,?3,?4,?5,?6)",
        params![t, id, column, parent_t, parent_id, if invalid {2} else {0}],
    )?;
    Ok(())
}
pub(super) fn capture_through_parent(
    tx: &Tx<'_>,
    name: &str,
    table: &Table,
    id: &str,
    column: &str,
    row: &Value,
) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    if let Some(through) = &table.through {
        if (through.fields.contains_key(column)
            || matches!(
                column,
                crate::schema::through::PARENT_DEADLINE | crate::schema::through::DEADLINE
            ))
            && let Ok(Value::Id(parent_id)) = row.field(&through.reference)
        {
            add_reference(tx, tx.num(name)?, id, column, &through.parent, parent_id)?;
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub(super) fn save_cell(
    tx: &Tx<'_>,
    name: &str,
    table: &Table,
    id: &str,
    column: &str,
    value: &Value,
    capture: bool,
) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    let t = tx.num(name)?;
    // @ref LLP 3000.014.000#implementation-proof-clarifications — another row cannot overwrite a cell's live origin.
    let live=table.engine_field(column) && table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|e|e.live.is_some());
    tx.conn().execute("INSERT INTO _dormant_values(t,id,column_name,data,live_source) VALUES(?1,?2,?3,?4,?5) ON CONFLICT(t,id,column_name) DO UPDATE SET data=excluded.data,live_source=excluded.live_source",params![t,id,column,canonical_json(value),i64::from(live)])?;
    if capture && !super::authority_origin::live_input(table,column) {
        capture_refs(tx, t, id, column, &table.columns[column], value)
            ));
        }
        Ok(out)
    }

    /// How many entries sit under `prefix`, counting at most `limit`.
    pub fn count_prefix(&self, table: &str, index_name: &str, prefix: &[Value], limit: u64) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        let ti = self.num(&format!("{table}.{index_name}"))?;
        let base = key::encode(prefix);
        let hi = key::upper_bound(&base);
        let count: i64 = self.tx.prepare_cached("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT 1 FROM i WHERE ti = ?1 AND k >= ?2 AND k < ?3 LIMIT ?4)")?.query_row(params![ti, base, hi, limit as i64], |row| row.get(0))?;
        Ok(count as u64)
    }

    /// Write a row image: a fresh insert when `old` is none, else a replace
    /// that touches only the index entries whose keys changed (a `words`
    /// index has one per token). Returns the number of entries written.
    pub fn put(&self, table_name: &str, table: &Table, row: &Value, old: Option<&Value>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        self.put_indexed(table_name, table, row, old, "INSERT INTO i(ti, k, id) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3)")
    }

    /// A replacement loader has already cleared the rows and created its
    /// temporary index heap. It must install those indexes before any read.
    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.4 — native replacement sorts complete indexes inside the publication transaction.
    pub fn put_loading_indexes(&self, table_name: &str, table: &Table, row: &Value) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        self.put_indexed(table_name, table, row, None, "INSERT INTO temp._device_index_load(ti, k, id) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3)")
    }

    fn put_indexed(&self, table_name: &str, table: &Table, row: &Value, old: Option<&Value>, insert_index: &str) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        self.clear_activation_scan();
        if table.ephemeral.is_some() { return Err(RuntimeError::Store("durable transaction cannot write an ephemeral table".into())); }
        let t = self.num(table_name)?;
        let id = row.field("id")?.as_str()?;
        narrowed::check_write(self,table_name,table,row,old)?;
        backfills::observe_write(self,t,id,table,row,old)?;
        let keys = crate::rows::index_write(table_name, table, row, old, id)?;
        self.changes.borrow_mut().record(table_name, table, old, Some(row));
        let data = canonical_json(row);
        let sql = if old.is_some() { "UPDATE r SET data = ?3 WHERE t = ?1 AND id = ?2" } else { "INSERT INTO r(t, id, data) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3)" };
        self.tx.prepare_cached(sql)?.execute(params![t, id, data])?;
        let mut insert = self.tx.prepare_cached(insert_index)?;
        let mut entries = 0;
        for crate::rows::IndexWrite { name, before, after } in keys {
            if before == after { continue; }
            let ti = self.num(&format!("{table_name}.{name}"))?;
            for key in before.iter().filter(|key| !after.contains(key)) {
                self.conn().prepare_cached("DELETE FROM i WHERE ti = ?1 AND k = ?2")?.execute(params![ti, key])?;
                entries += 1;
            }
            for key in after.iter().filter(|key| !before.contains(key)) {
                insert.execute(params![ti, key, id])?;
                entries += 1;
            }
        }
        entries += self.update_cap_counts(table_name, table, old, Some(row))?;
        Ok(entries)
    }

    pub fn delete(&self, table_name: &str, table: &Table, old: &Value) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        self.clear_activation_scan();
        if table.ephemeral.is_some() { return Err(RuntimeError::Store("durable transaction cannot write an ephemeral table".into())); }
        let t = self.num(table_name)?;
        self.changes.borrow_mut().record(table_name, table, Some(old), None);
        let id = old.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
        dormant::delete(self,t,&id,table_name)?;
        self.conn().prepare_cached("DELETE FROM r WHERE t = ?1 AND id = ?2")?.execute(params![t, id])?;
        let mut entries = 0;
        for (index_name, index) in &table.indexes {
            let ti = self.num(&format!("{table_name}.{index_name}"))?;
            for key in stored_index_keys(table, index, old, &id) {
                self.conn().prepare_cached("DELETE FROM i WHERE ti = ?1 AND k = ?2")?.execute(params![ti, key])?;
                entries += 1;
            }
        }
        entries += self.update_cap_counts(table_name, table, Some(old), None)?;
        Ok(entries)
    }

    pub fn next_seq(&self) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        Ok(self.tx.prepare_cached("SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq), 0) + 1 FROM _commits")?.query_row([], |row| row.get::<_, i64>(0))? as u64)
    }

    /// A meta key written with the transaction (a device's watermark lands
    /// with the rows it covers).
    pub fn set_meta(&self, key: &str, value: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.conn().execute("INSERT INTO _meta(key, value) VALUES (?1, ?2) ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value", params![key, value])?;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn meta(&self, key: &str) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError> {
        Ok(self.tx.prepare_cached("SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key = ?1")?.query_row([key], |row| row.get(0)).optional()?)
    }

    pub fn record_commit(&self, seq: u64, at: i64, program: &str, principal: &str, kind: &str, touched: &[String], writes: u64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        if !self.changes.borrow().covers(touched) { self.changes.borrow_mut().widen(); }
        self.conn().execute("INSERT INTO _change_evidence(seq, footprint) VALUES (?1, ?2)", params![seq as i64, canonical_json(&self.changes.borrow().footprint())])?;
    pub fn prune_dormant(
        &mut self,
        confirm: bool,
        expected_revision: Option<u64>,
    ) -> Result<serde_json::Value, RuntimeError> {
        let tx = self.transaction()?;
        let held = tx
            .meta("release_revision")?
            .and_then(|v| v.parse::<u64>().ok())
            .unwrap_or(0);
        if expected_revision.is_some_and(|n| n != held) {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Generation(
                "release revision changed; run releases and retry prune".into(),
            ));
        }
        let items = inventory(tx.conn(), None, usize::MAX)?;
        if !confirm {
            tx.rollback()?;
            return Ok(
                serde_json::json!({"pruned":false,"items":items,"rewrite":"snapback4 prune <dir> --allow-destructive"}),
            );
        }
        if !present(tx.conn())? {
            tx.rollback()?;
            return Ok(serde_json::json!({"pruned":true,"items":[],"revision":held}));
        }
        // Release only dormant homes; active application data is untouched.
        tx.conn().execute("UPDATE _assets SET released_at=COALESCE(released_at,?1) WHERE home_table IN (SELECT table_name FROM _dormant_tables) OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_values v JOIN _catalog c ON c.num=v.t WHERE c.name=_assets.home_table AND v.column_name=_assets.home_column AND v.id=_assets.home_id)",[crate::now_ms()])?;
        if super::narrowed::present(tx.conn())? {
            tx.conn().execute("UPDATE _assets SET released_at=COALESCE(released_at,?1) WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_narrow_rows n JOIN _catalog c ON c.num=n.t WHERE c.name=_assets.home_table AND n.id=_assets.home_id)",[crate::now_ms()])?;
            tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _dormant_values WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_narrow_rows n WHERE n.t=_dormant_values.t AND n.id=_dormant_values.id)",[])?;
            tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _dormant_narrow_rows",[])?;
        }
        let revision = event(
            &tx,
            "prune",
            tx.meta("release")?.and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()),
            None,
            serde_json::json!({"dropped_items":items.len(),"bytes":items.iter().map(|i|i.bytes).sum::<u64>(),"asset_bytes":items.iter().map(|i|i.asset_bytes).sum::<u64>()}),
            &items,
        )?;
        let event_id = tx.conn().last_insert_rowid();
        super::backfills::prune(&tx)?;
        tx.conn().execute_batch("DELETE FROM _dormant_values;DELETE FROM _dormant_rows;DELETE FROM _dormant_refs;DELETE FROM _dormant_columns;DELETE FROM _dormant_indexes;DELETE FROM _dormant_tables;")?;
        tx.commit()?;
        Ok(serde_json::json!({"pruned":true,"items":items,"revision":revision,"event":event_id}))
    }
}

                } else if let Some(position)=step.path.strip_prefix("maintains[").and_then(|s|s.strip_suffix(']')).and_then(|s|s.parse::<usize>().ok()) {
                    schema.maintains.get(position).map_or_else(||"view".into(),|m|m.label())
                } else {"backend".into()};
                let message=format!("{label} changed");
                if !report.changes.contains(&message){report.changes.push(message);}
            }
        }

        report.phase("preflight", &mut phase);
        if rebuilding {
            // @ref LLP 3000.000#implementation-follow-up — keys are still evaluated,
            // admitted and published in this transaction. Spill the key stream to
            // SQLite's temporary store, then insert in B-tree order instead of
            // repeatedly dirtying scattered main-database pages for every row.
        self.unsafe_dev_doors || !(bound.schema.auth.password && !bound.schema.auth.guests)
    }
    // Revalidate under the writer: neither a slow body nor an adoption queue
    // may carry fixture authority into a newly password-only schema.
    pub(crate) fn dev_authority(&self, engine: &Engine) -> Result<(), Refusal> {
        if self.personas && (self.unsafe_dev_doors || !(engine.schema().auth.password && !engine.schema().auth.guests)) { Ok(()) }
        else { Err(dev_doors::closed()) }
    }
    pub fn now(&self) -> i64 { lock(&self.clock).now().max(self.time_audience_clock.load(Ordering::Acquire)) }
    pub(crate) fn refresh_time_audience_clock(&self, engine: &Engine, now: i64) {
        if engine.schema().tables.values().any(|table| table.not_before.is_some()) {
            let durable = engine.store().meta("time_audience_clock").ok().flatten()
                .and_then(|value| value.parse::<i64>().ok()).unwrap_or(i64::MIN);
            self.time_audience_clock.fetch_max(now.max(durable), Ordering::AcqRel);
        } else {
            self.time_audience_clock.store(i64::MIN, Ordering::Release);
        }
    }
    fn advance_time_audiences(&self) -> Result<i64, snapback4_core::RuntimeError> {
        let requested = lock(&self.clock).now();
        // Non-timed reader traffic must retain its independent reader lane,
        // including while adoption or a mutation deliberately holds the writer.
        if self.time_audience_clock.load(Ordering::Acquire) == i64::MIN { return Ok(requested); }
        let mut engine = lock(&self.engine);
            lock(&shared.following).reclaim(shared.now(), snapback4_core::Ceilings { heap_bytes: 1 << 20, ..Default::default() });
            if let Err(error) = timely(&shared, tick) { snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: maintenance failed: {error}"); }
        }
        promote_aged(&shared, Instant::now());
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
    }
}

fn promote_aged(shared: &Shared, now: Instant) {
    if lock(&shared.maintenance).eligible(now, true) { bulk_slice(shared, true); }
}

pub(super) fn bulk(shared: Arc<Shared>) {
    loop {
        if crate::lifecycle::stopping() { return; }
        let observed = *lock(&shared.seq);
        let mut did_work = false;
        for _ in 0..3 {
            if crate::lifecycle::stopping() { return; }
            did_work |= bulk_slice(&shared, false);
            let pause = lock(&shared.maintenance).resume_at.saturating_duration_since(Instant::now());
            if !pause.is_zero() {
                // No shared lock survives this pause. Request commits do not
                // cancel repayment; empty kinds do not idle an active cycle.
                std::thread::sleep(pause.min(Duration::from_millis(100)));
            }
        }
        if !did_work {
            loop {
                let pause = lock(&shared.maintenance).empty_cycle(Instant::now());
                if pause.is_zero() { break; }
                std::thread::sleep(pause.min(Duration::from_millis(100)));
            }
            let seq = lock(&shared.seq);
            if *seq == observed {
                drop(shared.committed.wait_timeout(seq, Duration::from_millis(100)).unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()));
            }
        }
    }
}

// Reset even when a debug/unwind request panics mid-drain. Engine poison
// recovery and durable work cursors retain the normal retry semantics.
struct Advancing<'a>(&'a Shared);
impl Drop for Advancing<'_> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let mut state = lock(&self.0.maintenance);
        state.advancing = false;
        state.next = BulkKind::Delivery;
    }
}

fn completed_drain(work: Work, stopping: bool) -> Result<Work, snapback4_core::Refusal> {
    if stopping {
        return Err(snapback4_core::Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_INTERRUPTED", "clock", "clock advanced, but host shutdown interrupted the drain; inspect queued work instead of repeating the advance").guide("clock"));
    }
    Ok(work)
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#4-staging-clock — staging grants clock control, never fixture or persona authority.
pub(super) fn staging(shared: &Shared) -> bool {
    lock(&shared.engine).store().meta("deployment_environment").ok().flatten().as_deref() == Some("staging")
}
fn clock_service(request: &Request, shared: &Shared) -> Result<Option<String>, snapback4_core::Refusal> {
    if shared.personas { return Ok(None); }
    if !staging(shared) { return Err(crate::dev_clock::release()); }
    match super::session_identity::principal_of(request,shared) {
        Ok((principal,kind,snapback4_core::identity::SessionScope::Full)) if kind == "service" && principal.starts_with("service:") => Ok(Some(principal)),
        _ => Err(snapback4_core::Refusal::new("E_AUTH", "auth", "staging clock control requires a full service token").guide("clock")),
    }
}

/// The retirement phase shared by activation and its read-only occupancy
/// preview. Selection and the predecessor deadline predicate live here once;
/// checking a candidate must not count a row this phase would remove.
pub(crate) struct Retirement<'a> {
    affected: Vec<(String, &'a Table)>,
    now: i64,
}

impl<'a> Retirement<'a> {
    pub(crate) fn new(next: &Schema, previous: &'a Schema, now: i64) -> Self {
        let affected = next
            .through_order()
            .into_iter()
            .filter_map(|name| {
                let next = &next.tables[&name];
                let old = previous.table(&name)?;
                Self::changes_lifetime(next,old).then_some((name, old))
            })
            .collect();
        Self { affected, now }
    }

    fn changes_lifetime(next:&Table,old:&Table) -> bool {
        next.through != old.through || next.through.is_some() && (next.expire != old.expire || next.expire.as_ref().is_some_and(|field|old.defaults.get(field)!=next.defaults.get(field)))
    }

    pub(crate) fn retires_image(next:&Table,old:&Table,row:&Value,now:i64) -> bool {
        (next.through!=old.through || next.expire!=old.expire || old.expire.as_ref().is_some_and(|field|old.defaults.get(field)!=next.defaults.get(field))) && old.expired(row,now)
    }

    pub(crate) fn affects(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.affected.iter().any(|(table, _)| table == name)
    }

    pub(crate) fn retires(&self, name: &str, row: &Value) -> bool {
        self.affected
            .iter()
            .find(|(table, _)| table == name)
            .is_some_and(|(_, old)| old.expired(row, self.now))
    }
}

/// Capture barrier for an authoritative adapter's uncommitted generation.
pub fn activate(
    tx: &dyn Rows,
    next: &Schema,
    previous: Option<&Schema>,
    now: i64,
) -> Result<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, u64>, RuntimeError> {
    activate_retained(tx, next, previous, now, &Default::default())
}
//! Preflight activation pages before owning their serialized row images.
use super::*;
use crate::{error::MeterKind, meter::{Ceilings, Cut, Meter}, rows::{adoption, word_heap as heap}};

pub(super) fn walk(tx: &Tx<'_>, table: i64, mut visit: impl FnMut(&str, Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    walk_metered(tx, table, adoption::Work::DECODE, None, |id, row, _| visit(id, row))
}

// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.24.1 — reserve stored bytes before fetching or decoding; page scratch stays live until consumed.
pub(super) fn walk_metered(tx: &Tx<'_>, table: i64, work: adoption::Work, scratch: Option<&dyn Fn(&Value) -> crate::value::InternalPrice>,
    visit: impl FnMut(&str, Value, &mut Meter) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    let checked=|row:&Value|Ok(scratch.map_or_else(crate::value::InternalPrice::zero,|f|f(row)));
    walk_metered_checked(tx,table,work,scratch.map(|_|&checked as &dyn Fn(&Value)->Result<crate::value::InternalPrice,RuntimeError>),visit)
}

/// Row-specific provenance can fail closed before any page callback runs.
pub(super) fn walk_metered_checked(tx: &Tx<'_>, table: i64, work: adoption::Work,
    scratch: Option<&dyn Fn(&Value)->Result<crate::value::InternalPrice,RuntimeError>>,
    mut visit: impl FnMut(&str, Value, &mut Meter) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    const PAGE: usize = 256;
    let mut after: Option<String> = None;
    loop {
        // One job meter per page, shared with contribution evaluation. Retain
        // the continuation's allowance across the page; reset only after all
        // its row images and callback scratch have been consumed and dropped.
        let mut meter = Meter::new(Ceilings::job(), Cut::Abort);
        meter.at("adopt stored rows");
        meter.heap(after.as_deref().map_or(0, heap::text))?;
        meter.once(crate::meter::HeapSite::SqliteColumns, 2 * tx.page_size)?;
        let page_mark = meter.mark();
        let mut limit = PAGE;
        let mut page = loop {
            limit = work.limit(&meter, limit);
            let sizes = if after.is_some() {
                "SELECT octet_length(id), octet_length(data) FROM r WHERE t = ?1 AND id > ?2 ORDER BY id LIMIT ?3"
            } else {
                "SELECT octet_length(id), octet_length(data) FROM r WHERE t = ?1 AND ?2 IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT ?3"
            };
            let (mut count, mut bytes) = (0, 0u64);
            {
                let mut statement = tx.tx.prepare_cached(sizes)?;
                let mut rows = statement.query(params![table, after, limit as i64])?;
                while let Some(row) = rows.next()? {
                    let id_bytes = row.get::<_, i64>(0)? as usize;
                    let data_bytes = row.get::<_, i64>(1)? as usize;
                    // Rust-owned text, two native payload copies, allocation
                    // headers and exact Vec slots. Length preflight borrows no
                    // overflow payload (the same SQLite convention as scans).
                    let next = bytes.saturating_add(3 * (heap::allocation(id_bytes) + heap::allocation(data_bytes)) + 64 + heap::slots::<(String, String)>(1));
                    // This first size estimate bounds the fetch; admission below
                    // also checks the actual decoder and contribution allowance.
                    if count > 0 && next > meter.ceilings.heap_bytes / 2 { break; }
                    meter.heap(next - bytes)?;
                    bytes = next;
                    count += 1;
                }
            }
            if count == 0 { return Ok(()); }
            let query = if after.is_some() {
                "SELECT id, data FROM r WHERE t = ?1 AND id > ?2 ORDER BY id LIMIT ?3"
            } else {
                "SELECT id, data FROM r WHERE t = ?1 AND ?2 IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT ?3"
            };
            let mut page = Vec::<(String, String)>::with_capacity(count);
            {
                let mut statement = tx.tx.prepare_cached(query)?;
                let mut rows = statement.query(params![table, after, count as i64])?;
                while let Some(row) = rows.next()? { page.push((row.get(0)?, row.get(1)?)); }
            }
            if adoption::page_fits_checked(page.iter().map(|(_, data)| data.as_str()), &mut meter, work, scratch)? { break page; }
            limit = (page.len() / 2).max(1);
            drop(page);
            meter.release_heap(page_mark.clone());
        };
        for (id, data) in &page {
            let row_mark = meter.mark();
            meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
            // Decode plus copy-on-write projection, optional materialization
            // and validation scratch. Contribution keys reserve more through
            // this same meter, on top of the still-resident complete page.
            adoption::charge(&mut meter, adoption::decode_bytes(data))?;
            let row = serde_json::from_str(data).map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
            visit(id, row, &mut meter)?;
            meter.release_heap(row_mark);
        }
        // Move the last ID into the next page's continuation, without an
        // unpriced clone. Drop every other fetched byte before releasing.
        after = page.pop().map(|row| row.0);
        drop(page);
        meter.release_heap(page_mark);
    }
}

pub(super) fn identity(conn: &Connection) -> Result<Identity, RuntimeError> {
    let mut statement = conn.prepare_cached("SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key = ?1")?;
    let mut get = |key| statement.query_row([key], |row| row.get(0)).optional();

impl Store {
    /// Install a device's schema. Server engines also supply their programs
    /// and derived-state builder through `activate` below.
    pub fn install(&mut self, schema: &Schema) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.activate(schema, None, false, |_, _| Ok(())).map(|_| ())
    }

    /// A device can discard an obsolete partition while atomically caching
    /// its replacement backend and reset watermark. It never migrates rows
    /// whose authority belongs to a previous server generation.
    pub fn install_device(&mut self, schema: &Schema, metadata: &BTreeMap<String, String>, reset: bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.install_device_checked(schema, metadata, reset, &BTreeMap::new())
    }

    pub fn install_device_checked(&mut self, schema: &Schema, metadata: &BTreeMap<String, String>, reset: bool, expected: &BTreeMap<String, Option<String>>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.install_device_checked_with(schema, metadata, reset, expected, |_| Ok(()))
    }

    /// Device-owned sidecar changes share the schema installation transaction.
    pub fn install_device_checked_with(&mut self, schema: &Schema, metadata: &BTreeMap<String, String>, reset: bool, expected: &BTreeMap<String, Option<String>>, prepare: impl FnOnce(&Tx<'_>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.install_device_checked_with_finish(schema, metadata, reset, expected, prepare, |_| {
            Ok(())
        })
    }

    /// Opening recovery and its final reads must finish before installation commits.
    pub fn install_device_checked_with_finish<R>(&mut self, schema: &Schema, metadata: &BTreeMap<String, String>, reset: bool, expected: &BTreeMap<String, Option<String>>, prepare: impl FnOnce(&Tx<'_>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>, finish: impl FnOnce(&Tx<'_>) -> Result<R, RuntimeError>,
    ) -> Result<R, RuntimeError> {
        let mut result = None;
        self.activate(schema, None, reset, |tx, _| {
            for (key, value) in expected {
                let held: Option<String> = tx.conn().query_row("SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key = ?1", [key], |row| {
                        row.get(0)
                    }).optional()?;
                if &held != value { return Err(RuntimeError::Generation("the backend adoption capture is obsolete; retry sync".into())); }
            }
            prepare(tx)?;
            for (key, value) in metadata {
                // A device metadata namespace reset shares backend installation's transaction.
                if key.ends_with(':') {
                    tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key >= ?1 AND key < ?2", params![key, format!("{key}\u{10ffff}")])?;
                } else { tx.set_meta(key, value)?; }
            }
            if reset { tx.conn().execute_batch("DELETE FROM _device_base; DELETE FROM _device_snapshot;")?; }
            result = Some(finish(tx)?);
            Ok(())
        })?;
        Ok(result.expect("activation ran opening recovery"))
    }

    pub(crate) fn activate(&mut self, schema: &Schema, programs: Option<&BTreeMap<String, Program>>, reset: bool, build: impl FnOnce(&Tx<'_>, bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        self.activate_at(schema, programs, reset, crate::now_ms(), |tx, changed, _| build(tx, changed))
    }

    pub(crate) fn activate_at(&mut self, schema: &Schema, programs: Option<&BTreeMap<String, Program>>, reset: bool, now: i64, build: impl FnOnce(&Tx<'_>, bool, &mut super::adoption_report::AdoptionReport) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        // One-shot device preparation is never retried or given a larger cache.
        self.activate_transaction(schema, programs, reset, now, true, build)
    }

    pub(crate) fn activate_at_with_launch<R>(&mut self, schema: &Schema, programs: Option<&BTreeMap<String, Program>>, reset: bool, now: i64, allow_launch: bool, check: impl Fn(&Connection) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>, mut build: impl FnMut(&Tx<'_>, bool, &mut super::adoption_report::AdoptionReport) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>, finish: impl Fn(&Tx<'_>) -> Result<R, RuntimeError>,
    ) -> Result<(u64, R), RuntimeError> {
        let budget = if programs.is_some() { super::activation_cache::configured_mib()? } else { 0 };
        // The server builder owns only transaction-local work. Recreate all of
        // it on retry, with the same schema/programs/activation time.
        self.with_activation_cache(budget, |store| {
            store.activate_transaction_with(schema, programs, reset, now, allow_launch, &check, &mut build, &finish)
        })
    }

    pub(super) fn activate_transaction(&mut self, schema: &Schema, programs: Option<&BTreeMap<String, Program>>, reset: bool, now: i64, allow_launch: bool, build: impl FnOnce(&Tx<'_>, bool, &mut super::adoption_report::AdoptionReport) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        self.activate_transaction_with(schema, programs, reset, now, allow_launch, |_| Ok(()), build, |_| Ok(())).map(|(generation, ())| generation)
    }

    fn activate_transaction_with<R>(&mut self, schema: &Schema, programs: Option<&BTreeMap<String, Program>>, reset: bool, now: i64, allow_launch: bool, check: impl FnOnce(&Connection) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>, build: impl FnOnce(&Tx<'_>, bool, &mut super::adoption_report::AdoptionReport) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>, finish: impl FnOnce(&Tx<'_>) -> Result<R, RuntimeError>,
    ) -> Result<(u64, R), RuntimeError> {
        // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#4-staging-clock — a removed opening boundary cannot lower durable source retirement time.
        let now=if self.server {now.max(self.meta("time_audience_clock")?.and_then(|s|s.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(i64::MIN))}else{now};
        super::live_activation::configure(&self.conn,schema)?;
        let mut report = super::adoption_report::AdoptionReport::default();
        let mut phase = std::time::Instant::now();
        if programs.is_some() {
            if let Some(estimate) = self.adoption_estimate(schema)?.filter(|e| e.seconds().1 > 1.0) {
                crate::diagnostic!("snapback4: atomic adoption: {}", estimate.summary());

            let estimates = self.check_timeline_activation_at(schema, now, allow_launch)?;
            for estimate in estimates.iter().filter(|e| e.sources != 0) { crate::diagnostic!("snapback4: atomic feed adoption: {}", estimate.summary()); }
        }
        report.phase("read-only advice", &mut phase);

impl Tx<'_> {
    pub(super) fn clear_activation_scan(&self) {
        if let Some(buffer) = &self.activation_scan {
            buffer.borrow_mut().take();
        }
    }

    /// None means use the ordinary adapter; Some(None) proves an empty range.
    /// No Value is decoded by read-ahead, so malformed/unvisited payloads do not
    /// change a caller's result or refusal. A too-wide first row uses the old path.
    pub(super) fn activation_head(
        &self,
        t: i64,
        ti: i64,
        lo: &[u8],
        hi: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<Option<Option<(String, Vec<u8>)>>, RuntimeError> {
        let Some(buffer) = &self.activation_scan else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let mut held = buffer.borrow_mut();
        if let Some(page) = held.as_mut() {
            if page.table == t && page.index == ti && page.hi == hi && lo >= page.lo.as_slice() {
                while page
                    .rows
                    .front()
                    .is_some_and(|(_, key)| key.as_slice() < lo)
                {
                    page.rows.pop_front();
                }
                if let Some(row) = page.rows.pop_front() {
                    // Only forward cursors may reuse the unread tail.
                    page.lo = crate::key::upper_bound(&row.1);
                    return Ok(Some(Some(row)));
                }
            }
        }
        held.take();
        const PAGE: usize = 32;
        const BYTES: u64 = 128 * 1024;
        let mut meter = Meter::new(
            Ceilings {
                heap_bytes: BYTES,
                ..Ceilings::job()
            },
            Cut::Abort,
        );
        meter.at("adopt serialized read-ahead");
        let fixed = heap::slots::<(String, Vec<u8>)>(PAGE)
            + heap::allocation(lo.len())
            + heap::allocation(hi.len())
            // upper_bound clones then appends: reserve the old cursor, clone,
            // and the Vec growth replacement together, including capacity.
            + 4 * heap::allocation(2 * crate::rows::MAX_INDEX_KEY_BYTES + 1)
            + 2 * self.page_size;
        // An unusually large SQLite page can simply disable this optimization.
        if !meter.room(crate::error::MeterKind::HeapBytes, fixed) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        meter.heap(fixed)?;
        let mut count = 0;
        {
            let mut statement = self.tx.prepare_cached("SELECT octet_length(r.data), length(i.k) FROM i JOIN r ON r.t = ?1 AND r.id = i.id WHERE i.ti = ?2 AND i.k >= ?3 AND i.k < ?4 ORDER BY i.k LIMIT 32")?;
            let mut rows = statement.query(params![t, ti, lo, hi])?;
            while let Some(row) = rows.next()? {
                let bytes = 3
                    * (heap::allocation(row.get::<_, i64>(0)? as usize)
                        + heap::allocation(row.get::<_, i64>(1)? as usize))
                    + 64;
                if !meter.room(crate::error::MeterKind::HeapBytes, bytes) {
                    break;
                }
                meter.heap(bytes)?;
                meter.charge(crate::error::MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
                count += 1;
            }
        }
        if count == 0 {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let mut page = Page {
            table: t,
            index: ti,
            lo: lo.to_vec(),
            hi: hi.to_vec(),
            rows: VecDeque::with_capacity(PAGE),
            _meter: meter,
        };
        {
            let mut statement = self.tx.prepare_cached(scan_sql(Dir::Asc))?;
            let mut rows = statement.query(params![t, ti, lo, hi, count])?;
            while let Some(row) = rows.next()? {
                page.rows.push_back((row.get(0)?, row.get(1)?));
            }
        }
        let first = page.rows.pop_front();
        if let Some((_, key)) = &first {
            page.lo = crate::key::upper_bound(key);
        }
        *held = Some(page);
        Ok(Some(first))
    }
}

//! Admission for a fetched adoption page, before any callback can write.
use crate::{error::{MeterKind, RuntimeError}, meter::Meter, schema::{ColumnDefault, IndexComponent, Maintain, Table}, value::{Value, InternalPrice}};
use super::word_heap as heap;
use crate::engine::authorized_scan::InternalLedger;

/// Cumulative callback work per source row. Admission adds one examination;
/// heap is checked separately because row scratch is released after each row.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct Work {
    pub examined: u64,
    pub steps: u64,
    pub index_entries: u64,
}

impl Work {
    pub const DECODE: Self = Self { examined: 1, steps: 0, index_entries: 0 };

    pub fn with_contribution(mut self, maintain: &Maintain) -> Self {
        self.examined = self.examined.saturating_add(1);
        self.steps = self.steps.saturating_add(maintain.evaluation_steps());
        // A selected contribution creates exactly one entry, otherwise none.
        self.index_entries = self.index_entries.saturating_add(1);
        self
    }

    pub fn table(table: &Table) -> Self {
        table.indexes.values().fold(Self::DECODE, |work, index| match index.components.first() {
            Some(IndexComponent::Contribution(maintain)) => work.with_contribution(maintain),
            _ => work,
        })
    }

    fn counters(self, meter: &Meter) -> [(MeterKind, u64, u64, u64); 3] {
        [
            (MeterKind::Examined, self.examined.saturating_add(1), meter.used.examined, meter.ceilings.examined),
            (MeterKind::Steps, self.steps, meter.used.steps, meter.ceilings.steps),
            (MeterKind::IndexEntries, self.index_entries, meter.used.index_entries, meter.ceilings.index_entries),
        ]
    }

    pub fn limit(self, meter: &Meter, maximum: usize) -> usize {
        self.counters(meter).into_iter().filter(|(_, per_row, _, _)| *per_row != 0)
            .fold(maximum as u64, |limit, (_, per_row, used, ceiling)| limit.min(ceiling.saturating_sub(used) / per_row))
            // An empty range is still legal; a non-fitting singleton refuses
            // in fits(), after establishing that there really is a source row.
            .max(1) as usize
    }

    fn fits(self, meter: &Meter, count: usize) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
        for (kind, per_row, used, ceiling) in self.counters(meter) {
            let actual = used.saturating_add(per_row.saturating_mul(count as u64));
            if actual > ceiling {
                if count > 1 { return Ok(false); }
                return Err(RuntimeError::Bound { kind, actual, ceiling, site: meter.site().to_owned() });
            }
        }
        Ok(true)
    }
}

pub(crate) fn decode_bytes(data: &str) -> InternalPrice {
    InternalLedger::with_meter(&mut Meter::new(crate::Ceilings::unbounded(), crate::meter::Cut::Abort), |_, scope| heap::stored_row(data, scope).fixed(4096))
}

/// The price remains opaque: adoption may charge it only on its internal meter.
pub(crate) fn contribution_bytes(row: &Value, table: &Table) -> InternalPrice {
    InternalLedger::with_meter(&mut Meter::new(crate::Ceilings::unbounded(), crate::meter::Cut::Abort), |_, scope| {
        let mut bytes = row.retained_internal(scope);
        for (name, kind) in &table.columns {
            if row.field(name).is_ok() { continue; }
            let added = if table.maintained.contains_key(name) || kind.is_optional() { Some(InternalPrice::zero()) }
                else if let Some(ColumnDefault::Literal(value)) = table.defaults.get(name) { Some(value.retained_internal(scope)) }
                else { None };
            if let Some(added) = added { bytes = bytes.fixed(80 + name.len() as u64).plus(added); }
        }
        bytes.times(4).fixed(4096)
    })
}

pub(crate) fn charge(meter: &mut Meter, price: InternalPrice) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    InternalLedger::with_meter(meter, |meter, scope| price.charge(meter, scope))
}
pub(crate) fn fits(meter: &mut Meter, price: &InternalPrice) -> bool {
    InternalLedger::with_meter(meter, |meter, scope| price.fits(meter, scope))
}

fn absence(tx:&Tx<'_>,t:i64,id:&str,key:&str)->Result<BTreeSet<String>,RuntimeError>{
    Ok(tx.conn().prepare("SELECT column_name FROM _backfill_absence WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2 AND definition=?3")?.query_map(params![t,id,key],|r|r.get(0))?.collect::<Result<_,_>>()?)
}
fn save(tx:&Tx<'_>,t:i64,id:&str,key:&str,e:&Evidence,active:bool)->Result<(),RuntimeError>{
    tx.conn().execute("INSERT INTO _backfill_evidence(t,id,definition,inputs,before_image,after_image,active,epoch) VALUES(?1,?2,?3,?4,?5,?6,?7,?8) ON CONFLICT(t,id,definition) DO UPDATE SET inputs=excluded.inputs,before_image=excluded.before_image,after_image=excluded.after_image,active=excluded.active,epoch=excluded.epoch",params![t,id,key,canonical_json(&e.inputs),canonical_json(&e.before),canonical_json(&e.after),active,e.epoch])?;
    tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _backfill_pruned WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2 AND definition=?3",params![t,id,key])?;
    tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _backfill_absence WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2 AND definition=?3",params![t,id,key])?;
    for c in &e.absent {tx.conn().execute("INSERT INTO _backfill_absence VALUES(?1,?2,?3,?4)",params![t,id,key,c])?;}
    Ok(())
}
pub(super) fn delete(tx:&Tx<'_>,t:i64,id:&str)->Result<(),RuntimeError>{
    if present(tx)? {
        tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _backfill_evidence WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2",params![t,id])?;
        tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _backfill_pruned WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2",params![t,id])?;
        tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _backfill_absence WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2",params![t,id])?;
    } Ok(())
}
// Never archive reference/asset preimages without lifetime evidence. New reference
// fields are safe: subsequent retirement is owned by the ordinary dormant ledger.
fn protected(kind:&crate::schema::ColumnType)->bool {
    use crate::schema::ColumnType::*;
    match kind {Optional(k)=>protected(k),Ref{..}|Image{..}|Video{..}|File{..}|List{..}|ListRange{..}=>true,_=>false}
}
pub(super) fn transition(tx:&Tx<'_>,next:&Schema,previous:Option<&Schema>,sources:&BTreeMap<String,Table>,now:i64,report:&mut super::adoption_report::AdoptionReport)->Result<(),RuntimeError>{
    if next.backfills.is_empty() && previous.is_none_or(|s|s.backfills.is_empty()) && !present(tx)? { return Ok(()); }
    enable(tx)?;
    for fill in &next.backfills { fill.admit(next).map_err(refusal)?; }
    // A name is immutable within a continuous lineage. Replacing a transform
    // deliberately goes through an old-source/bridge transition first.
    if let Some(old)=previous {for f in &next.backfills {if old.backfills.iter().any(|p|p.table==f.table && p.name==f.name && p.key()!=f.key()) {return Err(refusal(format!("backfill {} {} changed; use a new name in a bridge release rather than replacing historical meaning",f.table,f.name)));}}}
    for fill in &next.backfills {
        tx.conn().execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO _backfill_definitions VALUES(?1,?2)",params![fill.key(),canonical_json(fill)])?;
    }
    let next_keys:BTreeSet<_>=next.backfills.iter().map(Backfill::key).collect();
    let definitions:Vec<Backfill>=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT definition FROM _backfill_definitions WHERE digest IN (SELECT definition FROM _backfill_evidence WHERE active=1 UNION SELECT definition FROM _backfill_pruned WHERE active=1) ORDER BY digest")?.query_map([],|r|r.get::<_,String>(0))?.map(|s|decode(&s?)).collect::<Result<_,RuntimeError>>()?;
    for fill in definitions.iter().rev().filter(|f|!next_keys.contains(&f.key())) {
        let Some(table)=next.table(&fill.table) else {continue};
        let t=tx.num(&fill.table)?;let key=fill.key();let mut bad=super::adopt_refusals::Samples::default();let mut count=0;
        super::activation::walk(tx,t,|id,mut row|{
            let Some(e)=evidence(tx,t,id,&key)? else {
                let pruned:bool=tx.conn().query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _backfill_pruned WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2 AND definition=?3 AND active=1)",params![t,id,key],|r|r.get(0))?;
                if pruned && fill.outputs.iter().any(|c|table.columns.contains_key(c)) {bad.add(id,"rollback preimage was explicitly pruned; select a bridge preserving current data or restore a backup");}
                return Ok(())
            };
            if !e.active {return Ok(())}
            let fields=match &mut row {Value::Row(f)|Value::Map(f)=>f,_=>return Err(refusal("invalid stored row"))};
            let mut changed=false;
            for c in &fill.outputs {if table.columns.contains_key(c) {
                let current=fields.get(c);let before=e.before.get(c);let after=e.after.get(c);
                if current!=after && current!=before {bad.add(id,&format!("{}.{} changed after backfill {}; keep a bridge and repair through an authorized mutation before rollback",fill.table,c,fill.name));return Ok(())}
                if let Some(value)=before {fields.insert(c.clone(),value.clone());}else{fields.remove(c);}
                changed=true;
            }}
            if changed {tx.conn().execute("UPDATE r SET data=?1 WHERE t=?2 AND id=?3",params![canonical_json(&row),t,id])?;count+=1;}
            save(tx,t,id,&key,&e,false)
        })?;
        if bad.count>0 {return Err(refusal(format!("backfill {} {} rollback: {}",fill.table,fill.name,bad.describe())))}
        if count>0 {report.backfills.push(format!("{} {} reversed on {count} {}",fill.table,fill.name,if count==1 {"row"}else{"rows"}));tx.set_meta("activation_population","true")?;}
    }
    let old_keys:BTreeSet<_>=previous.into_iter().flat_map(|s|s.backfills.iter().map(Backfill::key)).collect();
    let restored_tables:BTreeSet<i64>=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT DISTINCT n.t FROM _dormant_narrow_rows n WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM r WHERE r.t=n.t AND r.id=n.id)")?.query_map([],|r|r.get(0))?.collect::<Result<_,_>>()?;
    let entering:Vec<_>=next.backfills.iter().filter(|f|!old_keys.contains(&f.key()) || tx.num(&f.table).is_ok_and(|t|restored_tables.contains(&t))).collect();
    if entering.is_empty(){return Ok(())}
    let populated = entering.iter().try_fold(false, |any,fill| -> Result<bool,RuntimeError> {
        Ok(any || tx.conn().query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM r WHERE t=?1)",[tx.num(&fill.table)?],|r|r.get::<_,bool>(0))?)
    })?;
    if !populated {return Ok(())}
    let mut source=previous.cloned().unwrap_or_default();source.tables=sources.clone();source.backfills.clear();
    // Point lookup indexes are rebuilt against the assembled source images,
    // including restored rows, before any output patch is applied.
    let mut reads=BTreeSet::new();
    for f in &entering {collect_reads(&f.program.body,&mut reads);}
    for (name,index) in &reads {
        let wanted=next.table(name).and_then(|t|t.index(&index)).ok_or_else(||refusal("backfill lookup index absent"))?;
        let old_table=source.tables.get_mut(name).ok_or_else(||refusal(format!("backfill lookup source {name} has no historical definition")))?;
        if !wanted.is_plain() || wanted.columns().iter().any(|c|c!="id" && !old_table.columns.contains_key(c)) {return Err(refusal(format!("backfill lookup {name}.{index} requires predecessor fields; use an indexed bridge")))}

    fn scan_metered(&self, table: &str, index_name: &str, prefix: &[Value], bounds: &Bounds, dir: Dir, limit: usize, scope: &crate::engine::Authorization, meter: &mut crate::engine::InternalMeter<'_>) -> Result<Vec<(Value, Vec<u8>)>, RuntimeError> {
        use crate::rows::word_heap as heap;
        // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.24.5 — the public charge is the shared logical one; SQLite's own scratch is guarded.
        heap::scan_open(meter, table, index_name, prefix, bounds, scope)?;
        let mut guard = heap::StoreGuard::open(meter, SCAN_MEMORY_GUARD);
        let Some((lo, hi)) = crate::rows::scan_range(prefix, bounds, dir) else { return Ok(Vec::new());
        };
        let t = self.num(table)?;
        let ti = self.num(&format!("{table}.{index_name}"))?;
        // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.24.1 — stream preflight allowances before stepping to the next row.
        // Per-execution statement storage and the page cache are shared images outside this ledger, as for every store scan; engine/word_heap/tests.rs::sqlite_empty_scan_statement_storage_is_pinned_and_transient pins the excluded execution storage.
        // Within one preflight execution the first row's resident copy (one
        // page_size buffer per column, two registers) precedes its guard
        // reservation; every later row's copy follows the previous row's.
        // The guard prepays that first copy. BYTELENARG / LENGTHARG never read
        // overflow payloads; Rust borrows the payload statement's JSON.
        guard.reserve(meter, 2 * self.page_size)?;
        if limit == 1 && dir == Dir::Asc
            && let Some(head) = self.activation_head(t, ti, &lo, &hi)? {
            let Some((data, key)) = head else { return Ok(Vec::new()); };
            let mut preflight = heap::Preflight::new();
            preflight.entry(meter, &mut guard, data.len() as u64, key.len() as u64, 64)?;
            let additional = heap::scan_entry(meter, &mut guard, 0, 0, &data, &key)?;
            let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(additional);
            out.push((serde_json::from_str(&data).map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?, key,
            ));
            return Ok(out);
        }
        let sizes = match dir {
            Dir::Asc => {
                "SELECT octet_length(r.data), length(i.k) FROM i JOIN r ON r.t = ?1 AND r.id = i.id WHERE i.ti = ?2 AND i.k >= ?3 AND i.k < ?4 ORDER BY i.k ASC LIMIT ?5"
            }
            Dir::Desc => {
                "SELECT octet_length(r.data), length(i.k) FROM i JOIN r ON r.t = ?1 AND r.id = i.id WHERE i.ti = ?2 AND i.k >= ?3 AND i.k < ?4 ORDER BY i.k DESC LIMIT ?5"
            }
        };
        let mut preflight = heap::Preflight::new();
        {
            let mut statement = self.tx.prepare_cached(sizes)?;
            let mut rows = statement.query(params![t, ti, lo, hi, limit as i64])?;
            // Refusal drops/resets this statement without stepping again.
            while let Some(row) = rows.next()? {
                // Two payload copies and two allocation headers/alignment per row.
                if !preflight.entry(meter, &mut guard, row.get::<_, i64>(0)? as u64, row.get::<_, i64>(1)? as u64, 64)? { break; }

//! A development reset: the adopted schema over an empty store, under a new
//! store identity, optionally reseeded, in one SQLite transaction.
// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.25 — what "fresh" keeps and what it empties; why the head keeps counting.
use super::*;

/// Tables a reset keeps whole: the store's own metadata, the catalog that
/// numbers tables and indexes, and the adopted generations.
const KEPT: [&str; 3] = ["_meta", "_catalog", "_generations"];

/// Identity tables a reset empties except for service seats: the dev
/// worker's session and `snapback4 token` seats outlive a reset, accounts,
/// guests and their sessions do not.
const SERVICE_SEATS: [(&str, &str); 5] = [
    ("_principals", "id"), ("_sessions", "principal"), ("_read_sessions", "principal"),
    ("_principal_generations", "principal"), ("_session_mint_bindings", "principal"),
];

/// What a development reset did. The caller unlinks `assets` after the
/// commit, outside any engine guard it holds.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct DevReset {
    pub previous_store_id: String,
    pub store_id: String,
    /// The store's head after the reset and any reseed.
    pub seq: u64,
    pub seeded: u64,
    pub assets: assets::AssetSweep,
}

impl Engine {
    /// Empty every application table and everything derived from them
    /// (views, maintained columns, indexes, counts, the partition log),
    /// every queue (effects, jobs, actions), uploaded assets and every
    /// non-service account and session; keep the adopted schema and
    /// generation. The store takes a new identity so a connected device
    /// re-acquires instead of keeping its partition; the head keeps counting
    /// (the reset is itself a commit). `rows` are then written as `/seed`
    /// writes them, in the same transaction. Development only: the release
    /// host never calls this.
    pub fn dev_reset_at(&mut self, rows: Vec<(String, Value)>, now: i64) -> Result<DevReset, RuntimeError> {
        // Like adoption: no ephemeral program runs across the identity change.
        drop(self.ephemeral.lock()?);
        let tx = self.store.transaction()?;
        // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.000.000#2-fixture-semantics — the new store identity must not inherit the retired store's future clock.
        tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key = 'time_audience_clock'", [])?;
        let now = time_audience::pin_writer_time(&self.schema, &tx, now)?;
        let previous_store_id = tx.meta("store_id")?.unwrap_or_default();
        let head = tx.next_seq()?.saturating_sub(1);
        let assets: Vec<String> = tx.conn().prepare("SELECT id FROM _assets")?.query_map([], |row| row.get(0))?.collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
        let tables: Vec<String> = tx.conn()
            .prepare("SELECT name FROM main.sqlite_schema WHERE type = 'table' AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite\\_%' ESCAPE '\\'")?
            .query_map([], |row| row.get(0))?.collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
        // @ref LLP 3000.039#6.5 — every table empties together: no referential action runs, and no reference is left naming a removed row.
        for table in &tables {
            if KEPT.contains(&table.as_str()) { continue; }
            let quoted = format!("\"{}\"", table.replace('"', "\"\""));
            match SERVICE_SEATS.iter().find(|(name, _)| name == table) {
                Some((_, column)) => tx.conn().execute(&format!("DELETE FROM {quoted} WHERE substr({column}, 1, ?2) <> ?1"),
                    rusqlite::params![crate::identity::SERVICE_PREFIX, crate::identity::SERVICE_PREFIX.len() as i64])?,
                None => tx.conn().execute(&format!("DELETE FROM {quoted}"), [])?,
            };
        }
        // Prime at the reset clock in this transaction: no old period fires,
        // and the next crossed boundary fires normally. Replay's count restarts.
        tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key LIKE 'schedule:%' OR key LIKE 'schedule-shape:%' OR key = 'dev:suppressed-effects'", [])?;
        for schedule in &self.schema.schedules {
            tx.set_meta(&format!("schedule:{}", schedule.name), &schedule.boundary(now).to_string())?;
            tx.set_meta(&format!("schedule-shape:{}", schedule.name), &crate::value::digest(schedule))?;
        }
        tx.conn().execute("UPDATE _meta SET value = lower(hex(randomblob(16))) WHERE key = 'store_id'", [])?;
        let store_id = tx.meta("store_id")?.unwrap_or_default();
        // Every table changed: no change evidence may certify an interval
        // across the reset.
        tx.changes.borrow_mut().widen();
        let touched: Vec<String> = self.schema.visible_tables().map(|(name, _)| name.clone()).collect();
        tx.record_commit(head + 1, now, "dev reset", crate::SYSTEM_PRINCIPAL, "reset", &touched, 0)?;
        let seeded = seed_rows(&self.schema, &tx, rows, now)?;
        let seq = tx.next_seq()?.saturating_sub(1);
        tx.commit()?;
        // A new store identity starts a fresh bounded expiry walk. Clear only
        // after commit so a refused reset keeps the old store's continuation.
        self.expiry_after.clear();
        self.timeline_schedule = timeline::Schedule::default();

        self.prediction_skips = self.schema.operations.get(&program.name)

            .map(|fact| fact.prediction_skips.iter().cloned().collect()).unwrap_or_default();

            for value in self.context.args.values() { self.meter.heap(value.expression_copy(ExpressionAccess(())))?; }
            self.statements(&program.body, &program.name)
        })();

        }

    pub fn count(&self, table: &str) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        self.check_ownership()?;
        let Some(t) = self.catalog.get(table) else { return Ok(0);
        };
        Ok(self.conn.prepare_cached("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM r WHERE t = ?1")?.query_row([t], |row| row.get::<_, i64>(0))? as u64)
    }

    /// What the store weighs, by part: the rows, their index entries, the
    /// partition log (one row per recipient per event), the op records,
    /// and the file. `doctor` prints it; the log's ratio to the rows is the
    /// amplification the per-recipient log costs.
    pub fn sizes(&self) -> Result<Sizes, RuntimeError> {
        self.check_ownership()?;
        let sum = |sql: &str| -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> { Ok(self.conn.query_row(sql, [], |row| row.get::<_, Option<i64>>(0))?.unwrap_or(0).max(0) as u64) };
        // Read-only inspection also works before the next writer migrates _ops.
        let columns: Vec<String> = self.conn.prepare("SELECT name FROM pragma_table_info('_ops')")?
            .query_map([], |row| row.get(0))?.collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
        let binding_sizes = ["name", "args_digest", "at"].into_iter().filter(|name| columns.iter().any(|column| column == name))
            .map(|name| format!(" + COALESCE(LENGTH({name}), 0)")).collect::<String>();
        Ok(Sizes {
            rows: sum("SELECT SUM(LENGTH(data) + LENGTH(id)) FROM r")?,
            row_count: sum("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM r")?,
            indexes: sum("SELECT SUM(LENGTH(k) + LENGTH(id)) FROM i")?,
            log: sum("SELECT SUM(COALESCE(LENGTH(data), 0) + LENGTH(id) + LENGTH(partition) + LENGTH(t)) FROM _log")?,
            log_events: sum("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM _log")?,
            ops: sum(&format!("SELECT SUM(LENGTH(outcome) + LENGTH(id) + LENGTH(principal) + LENGTH(seq){binding_sizes}) FROM _ops"))?,
            file: sum("SELECT page_count * page_size FROM pragma_page_count(), pragma_page_size()")?,
        })
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize)]
pub struct Sizes {
    pub rows: u64,
    pub row_count: u64,
    pub indexes: u64,
    pub log: u64,
    pub log_events: u64,
    pub ops: u64,
    pub file: u64,
}

impl Sizes {
    /// The log's bytes per byte of rows.
    pub fn amplification(&self) -> f64 {
        if self.rows == 0 { 0.0 } else { self.log as f64 / self.rows as f64 }
    }
}

impl<'a> Tx<'a> {
    pub fn conn(&self) -> &Connection {
        self.clear_activation_scan();
        &self.tx
    }

    pub fn commit(self) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.tx.commit()?;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn rollback(self) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.tx.rollback()?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// A savepoint, so a program can roll back its own writes and keep the
    /// enclosing bookkeeping (a refused mutation still records its outcome).
    pub fn savepoint(&self, name: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.conn().execute_batch(&format!("SAVEPOINT {name}"))?;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn release(&self, name: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.conn().execute_batch(&format!("RELEASE {name}"))?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Roll back the named savepoint and release it in the same operation.
    pub fn rollback_to(&self, name: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.clear_activation_scan();
        self.changes.borrow_mut().widen();
        self.conn().execute_batch(&format!("ROLLBACK TO {name}; RELEASE {name}"))?;
        // Lazy sequence-table creation may have belonged to this savepoint.
        self.sequence_table.set(None);
        Ok(())
    }
//! A continuation belongs to a returned page, not the last auxiliary scan.
//! This retains the SB2 return/alias/one-to-one-shape analysis without its
//! certificate or receipt machinery.
use crate::ir::*;
use crate::Value;
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Origin {
    Empty,
    Page(String, Option<String>),
    Record(BTreeMap<String, Origin>),
    Cursor(String),
}
type Bindings = BTreeMap<String, Origin>;

#[path = "page_collectors.rs"]
mod collectors;

// @ref LLP 3000.002#proposed-device-representation-and-codec-redesign — only Postgres can prefetch; other stores keep no physical plan.
#[cfg(feature = "postgres")]
#[path = "prefetch.rs"]
mod prefetch;


#[derive(Clone)]
pub(super) struct Shape {
    pub page: String,
    pub targets: Vec<String>,
}

pub(super) struct ReturnedPage {
    pub page: String,
    pub shapes: BTreeSet<String>,
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub(super) struct Plan {
    pub returns: BTreeMap<String, ReturnedPage>,
    pub shapes: BTreeMap<String, Shape>,
    pub collectors: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    // Static compact sites and their execution counts; no IR/payload copies.
    #[cfg(feature = "server-search")]
    pub compact: BTreeMap<String, Option<usize>>,
    #[cfg(feature = "postgres")]
    pub prefetch: prefetch::Plan,
}

pub(super) fn plan(program: &Program, schema: &crate::schema::Schema, prefetch_enabled: bool) -> Plan {
    #[cfg(not(feature = "postgres"))]
    let _ = (schema, prefetch_enabled);
    #[cfg(feature = "postgres")]
    let prefetch = if prefetch_enabled { prefetch::plan(program).admit(schema) } else { prefetch::Plan::default() };
    if program.kind != ProgramKind::Query { return Plan { #[cfg(feature = "postgres")] prefetch, ..Plan::default() }; }
    let mut collectors = BTreeMap::new();
    let mut returns = crate::small_map::collect(returned_origins(program, false, &mut collectors).into_iter().filter_map(|(path, origin)|
        result_page(&origin).map(|(site, _)| (path, ReturnedPage { page: site.to_owned(), shapes: BTreeSet::new() }))));
    let mut shapes = BTreeMap::new();
    // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.6 — only the binder's returned shape can trim and select a rewind; ordinary origins stay main's.
    for (index, pair) in program.body.windows(2).enumerate() {
        let path = format!("{}:{}", program.name, index + 1);
        let Some(page) = program.returned_shapes.get(&path) else { continue; };
        let [Stmt::For { body, .. }, Stmt::Return(Expr::Variable(target))] = pair else { continue; };
        if !matches!(body.last(), Some(Stmt::Push { target: pushed, .. }) if pushed == target) { continue; }
        shapes.insert(path.clone(), Shape { page: page.clone(), targets: vec![target.clone()] });
        returns.insert(format!("{}:{}", program.name, index + 2), ReturnedPage { page: page.clone(), shapes: BTreeSet::from([path]) });
    }
    if !collectors.is_empty() {
        let flow = collectors::returned_collectors(program);
        collectors.retain(|path, _| flow.returned.contains(path) || !flow.visited.contains(path));
    }
    Plan { returns, collectors, shapes,
        #[cfg(feature = "server-search")]
        compact: crate::search_plan::merges(&program.body).into_iter()
            .filter(|merge| crate::search_plan::eligible(schema, merge))
            .map(|merge| (merge.site.clone(), None)).collect(),
        #[cfg(feature = "postgres")] prefetch }
}

    fn collect(origin: Origin, sites: &mut BTreeSet<String>) {

        for origin in returned_origins(program, true, &mut BTreeMap::new()).into_values() {
            collect(origin, &mut sites);
        }
        for origin in returned_origins(program, false, &mut BTreeMap::new()).into_values() {
            if let Some((site, _)) = result_page(&origin) {
                sites.insert(site.to_owned());

//! Database-authoritative release history and explicit dormant pruning.
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#4-explicit-pruning-and-audit — no implicit collector or unaudited data loss.
use super::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct DormantItem {
    /// Stable cursor; column/index names may coincide.
    pub key: String,
    pub path: String,
    pub kind: String,
    pub action: String,
    pub rows: u64,
    pub bytes: u64,
    pub asset_bytes: u64,
    /// Internal audit distinction: zero standalone cells may still be covered by a dormant row.
    #[serde(skip)]
    pub(crate) definition_only: bool,
    pub sample_ids: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default,skip_serializing_if="Option::is_none")]
    pub before_rows:Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default,skip_serializing_if="Option::is_none")]
    pub after_rows:Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default,skip_serializing_if="Option::is_none")]
    pub restored_rows:Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default,skip_serializing_if="Option::is_none")]
    pub before_sample_ids:Option<Vec<String>>,
}

impl DormantItem {
    pub fn unit(&self) -> &'static str {
        match (self.kind.as_str(), self.rows) { ("backfill", 1) => "preimage", ("backfill", _) => "preimages", ("column", 1) => "cell", ("column", _) => "cells", ("index", 1) => "entry", ("index", _) => "entries", (_, 1) => "row", _ => "rows" }
    }
}

impl Store {
    /// Values presently in active rows, independently of table population or other columns.
    pub fn rollback_incompatible_values(&self, current: &Schema, target: &Schema, name: &str, column: &str) -> Result<(u64, Vec<String>), RuntimeError> {
        let tx = self.authority_transaction()?;
        let table = &target.tables[name];
        let kind = &table.columns[column];
        if table.engine_field(column) || table.maintained.contains_key(column) { return Ok((0, Vec::new())); }
        let mut count = 0;
        let mut samples = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
        let mut statement = tx.conn().prepare("SELECT data FROM r WHERE t=(SELECT num FROM _catalog WHERE name=?1) ORDER BY id")?;
        for data in statement.query_map([name], |r| r.get::<_, String>(0))? {
            let mut row: Value = serde_json::from_str(&data?).map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
            crate::schema::materialize_optional_fields(&mut row, &current.tables[name]);
            if let Ok(value) = row.field(column)
                && super::narrowed::incompatible_column(&tx, table, name, column, kind, value)? {
                count += 1;
                if samples.len() < 5 {
                    let text = match value { Value::String(s) => format!("'{}'", s.replace('\\', "\\\\").replace('\'', "\\'").replace('\n', "\\n").replace('\r', "\\r")), _ => canonical_json(value) };
                    samples.insert(super::adopt_refusals::bounded(&text));
                }
            }
        }
        Ok((count, samples.into_iter().collect()))
    }
}

fn sql_number(n: u64) -> Result<i64, RuntimeError> {
    i64::try_from(n).map_err(|_| {
        RuntimeError::Generation("release counter exceeds SQLite integer range".into())
    })
}

        [],

    )?)
