            let selector=match kind.as_str(){
                "rows"=>"EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_narrow_rows n WHERE n.t=?3 AND n.id=_assets.home_id)",
                "column"=>"EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_values v JOIN r ON r.t=v.t AND r.id=v.id WHERE v.t=?3 AND v.id=_assets.home_id AND v.column_name=_assets.home_column)",
                _=>"EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_rows d WHERE d.t=?3 AND d.id=_assets.home_id)",
            };
            conn.query_row(&format!("SELECT COALESCE(SUM(bytes),0) FROM _assets WHERE home_table=?1 AND (?2 IS NULL OR home_column=?2) AND released_at IS NULL AND {selector}"),params![name,if kind=="table" || kind=="rows" {None}else{column.as_deref()},t],|r|r.get::<_,i64>(0).map(|n|n as u64))?
        };
        let definition_only = if kind == "column" {
            !conn.query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_values WHERE t=?1 AND column_name=?2)", params![t, column], |r| r.get::<_, bool>(0))?
        } else { count == 0 };
        out.push(DormantItem {
            key: format!("{kind}:{path}"),
            path,
            kind,
            action: "dormant".into(),
            rows: count,
            bytes,
            asset_bytes,
            definition_only,
            sample_ids: ids,
            before_rows:None,after_rows:None,restored_rows:None,before_sample_ids:None,
        });
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// Retained definitions represent logical entries, rebuilt on restoration.
/// A words index has zero or many entries per image; a row count is not its size.
//! Release-only storage outside the active row/index namespace.
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#2-retain-by-default — moves, restorations and deletion evidence share activation's transaction.
use super::*;
use crate::schema::{ColumnDefault, ColumnType, materialize_optional_fields};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

pub(crate) const VERSION: &str = "snapback4-release-store-3";

#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct Column {
    kind: ColumnType,
    default: Option<ColumnDefault>,
    authoritative: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    capture_source: Option<Table>,
}

pub(crate) fn enable(conn: &Connection) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    conn.execute_batch("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _dormant_narrow_rows(t INTEGER NOT NULL,id TEXT NOT NULL,data TEXT NOT NULL,definition TEXT NOT NULL,reason TEXT NOT NULL,PRIMARY KEY(t,id)) WITHOUT ROWID;
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _dormant_tables(table_name TEXT PRIMARY KEY, definition TEXT NOT NULL);
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _dormant_rows(t INTEGER NOT NULL,id TEXT NOT NULL,data TEXT NOT NULL,PRIMARY KEY(t,id)) WITHOUT ROWID;
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _dormant_columns(table_name TEXT NOT NULL,column_name TEXT NOT NULL,definition TEXT NOT NULL,PRIMARY KEY(table_name,column_name)) WITHOUT ROWID;
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _dormant_values(t INTEGER NOT NULL,id TEXT NOT NULL,column_name TEXT NOT NULL,data TEXT NOT NULL,live_source INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,PRIMARY KEY(t,id,column_name)) WITHOUT ROWID;
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _dormant_indexes(table_name TEXT NOT NULL,index_name TEXT NOT NULL,definition TEXT NOT NULL,PRIMARY KEY(table_name,index_name)) WITHOUT ROWID;
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _dormant_refs(t INTEGER NOT NULL,id TEXT NOT NULL,column_name TEXT NOT NULL,parent_t INTEGER NOT NULL,parent_id TEXT NOT NULL,invalid INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,PRIMARY KEY(t,id,column_name,parent_t,parent_id)) WITHOUT ROWID;
        CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS _dormant_parent ON _dormant_refs(parent_t,parent_id);
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _release_events(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,at INTEGER NOT NULL,operation TEXT NOT NULL,release INTEGER,previous INTEGER,generation INTEGER NOT NULL,revision INTEGER NOT NULL,summary TEXT NOT NULL);
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _release_event_items(event INTEGER NOT NULL,path TEXT NOT NULL,detail TEXT NOT NULL,PRIMARY KEY(event,path)) WITHOUT ROWID;")?;
    if !live_cells_column(conn)? {
        // Published predecessors have captured-only cells. Defaulting them
        // to captured is conservative; shared definitions cannot prove a
        // particular retained cell ever had live authority.
        conn.execute_batch("ALTER TABLE _dormant_values ADD COLUMN live_source INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;")?;
    }
    conn.execute("UPDATE _meta SET value=?1 WHERE key='version' AND value!='snapback4-release-store-4'", [VERSION])?;
    Ok(())
}

pub(super) fn live_cells_column(conn:&Connection)->Result<bool,RuntimeError> {
    Ok(conn.query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM pragma_table_info('_dormant_values') WHERE name='live_source')",[],|r|r.get(0))?)
}

pub(super) fn enabled(tx: &Tx<'_>) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
    Ok(matches!(tx.meta("version")?.as_deref(),Some(VERSION|"snapback4-release-store-2"|super::backfills::VERSION)))
}

fn authoritative(table: &Table, column: &str) -> bool {
    !table.maintained.contains_key(column) && !table.engine_field(column)
}

pub(super) fn definition(tx: &Tx<'_>, name: &str, table: &Table, column: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    let value = Column {
        kind: table.columns[column].clone(),
        default: table.defaults.get(column).cloned(),
        authoritative: authoritative(table, column),
        capture_source: table.engine_field(column).then(||table.clone()),
    };
    tx.conn().execute("INSERT INTO _dormant_columns VALUES(?1,?2,?3) ON CONFLICT(table_name,column_name) DO UPDATE SET definition=excluded.definition", params![name,column,canonical_json(&value)])?;
    Ok(())
}

fn references(kind: &ColumnType, value: &Value, out: &mut Vec<(String, String)>) {
    match (kind, value) {
        (ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) => references(inner, value, out),
        (ColumnType::List { of, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) => {
            for value in values {
                references(of, value, out);
            }
        }
        (ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(id)) => out.push((table.clone(), id.clone())),
        _ => {}
    }
}

fn rewrite_legacy_reference(
    kind: &ColumnType,
    value: &mut Value,
    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
) -> bool {
    match (kind, value) {
        (ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(id)) => {
            let Some(next) = ids.get(table).and_then(|ids| ids.get(id)) else { return false };
            *id = next.clone();
            true
        }
        (ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) => rewrite_legacy_reference(inner, value, ids),
        (ColumnType::List { of, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
            values.iter_mut().fold(false, |changed, value| rewrite_legacy_reference(of, value, ids) || changed),
        _ => false,
    }
}

fn rewrite_legacy_row(
    table: &Table,
    row: &mut Value,
    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
) -> bool {
    let (Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields)) = row else { return false };
    table.columns.iter().fold(false, |changed, (column, kind)| {
        fields.get_mut(column).is_some_and(|value| rewrite_legacy_reference(kind, value, ids)) || changed
    })
}

/// Rewrite references retained outside the active namespace alongside their
/// active counterparts. References whose aggregate target was itself retired
/// have no map and retain the ordinary dormant-lifetime refusal on restore.
// @ref LLP 3000.007.003#3.0 — identity adoption covers every surviving typed reference, including dormant storage.
pub(crate) fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(
    tx: &Tx<'_>,
    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
    if ids.values().all(BTreeMap::is_empty) || !enabled(tx)? { return Ok(0); }
    let mut rewritten = 0_u64;

    let cells = tx.conn().prepare(
        "SELECT v.t,v.id,v.column_name,v.data,c.definition FROM _dormant_values v JOIN _catalog k ON k.num=v.t JOIN _dormant_columns c ON c.table_name=k.name AND c.column_name=v.column_name ORDER BY v.t,v.id,v.column_name"
    )?.query_map([], |row| Ok((row.get::<_,i64>(0)?, row.get::<_,String>(1)?, row.get::<_,String>(2)?, row.get::<_,String>(3)?, row.get::<_,String>(4)?)))?
        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()?;
    for (t, id, column, data, definition) in cells {
        let definition: Column = serde_json::from_str(&definition).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
        let mut value: Value = serde_json::from_str(&data).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
        if rewrite_legacy_reference(&definition.kind, &mut value, ids) {
            tx.conn().execute("UPDATE _dormant_values SET data=?1 WHERE t=?2 AND id=?3 AND column_name=?4", params![canonical_json(&value),t,id,column])?;
            rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(1);
        }
    }

    let rows = tx.conn().prepare(
        "SELECT r.t,r.id,r.data,d.definition FROM _dormant_rows r JOIN _catalog c ON c.num=r.t JOIN _dormant_tables d ON d.table_name=c.name ORDER BY r.t,r.id"
    )?.query_map([], |row| Ok((row.get::<_,i64>(0)?, row.get::<_,String>(1)?, row.get::<_,String>(2)?, row.get::<_,String>(3)?)))?
        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()?;
    for (t, id, data, definition) in rows {
        let table: Table = serde_json::from_str(&definition).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
        let mut row: Value = serde_json::from_str(&data).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
        if rewrite_legacy_row(&table, &mut row, ids) {
            tx.conn().execute("UPDATE _dormant_rows SET data=?1 WHERE t=?2 AND id=?3", params![canonical_json(&row),t,id])?;
            rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(1);
        }
    }

    let narrowed = if super::narrowed::present(tx.conn())? {
        tx.conn().prepare(
            "SELECT t,id,data,definition FROM _dormant_narrow_rows ORDER BY t,id"
        )?.query_map([], |row| Ok((row.get::<_,i64>(0)?, row.get::<_,String>(1)?, row.get::<_,String>(2)?, row.get::<_,String>(3)?)))?
            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()?
    } else { Vec::new() };
    for (t, id, data, definition) in narrowed {
        let table: Table = serde_json::from_str(&definition).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
        let mut row: Value = serde_json::from_str(&data).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
        if rewrite_legacy_row(&table, &mut row, ids) {
            tx.conn().execute("UPDATE _dormant_narrow_rows SET data=?1 WHERE t=?2 AND id=?3", params![canonical_json(&row),t,id])?;
            rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(1);
        }
    }

    for (target, target_ids) in ids {
        if target_ids.is_empty() { continue; }
        let parent_t = tx.num(target)?;
        for (old, next) in target_ids {
            tx.conn().execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO _dormant_refs(t,id,column_name,parent_t,parent_id,invalid) SELECT t,id,column_name,parent_t,?1,invalid FROM _dormant_refs WHERE parent_t=?2 AND parent_id=?3", params![next,parent_t,old])?;
            tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _dormant_refs WHERE parent_t=?1 AND parent_id=?2", params![parent_t,old])?;
        }
    }
    Ok(rewritten)
}

    tx: &Tx<'_>,
    t: i64,

//! Human preview groups facts about one affected table/operation once.
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#15-wave-15-preview-and-rollback-day5 — full evidence remains available in JSON and verbose output.
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use snapback4_core::{Schema, ir::Program, store::DormantItem, successor::Step};
struct Group { warnings: Vec<String>, notes: Vec<String>, priority: u8 }
impl Default for Group { fn default() -> Self {Self {warnings:Vec::new(),notes:Vec::new(),priority:2}} }
fn table_prefix(text: &str, tables: &BTreeSet<String>) -> Option<String> {
    tables.iter().filter(|name|text.strip_prefix(name.as_str()).is_some_and(|tail|tail.is_empty() || tail.starts_with(['.',':',' ']))).max_by_key(|name|name.len()).cloned()
}
fn subject(text: &str, tables: &BTreeSet<String>, programs: &BTreeMap<String,Program>) -> String {
    // Read only generated subject positions, never arbitrary words inside an
    // authored predicate/refusal/value. Unknown formats remain release facts.
    if let Some(table)=table_prefix(text,tables) {return table;}
    for marker in ["table ","dependent ","backfill: "] {
        if let Some(tail)=text.strip_prefix(marker) && let Some(table)=table_prefix(tail,tables) {return table;}
    }
    let prefix=text.split(';').next().unwrap_or(text);
    if text.starts_with("queries/counts ") && let Some((_,tail))=prefix.split_once(" read ") && let Some(table)=table_prefix(tail,tables) {return table;}
    if text.starts_with("release ") && let Some((_,tail))=prefix.split_once(" safety dependencies on ") && let Some(table)=table_prefix(tail,tables) {return table;}
    if text.starts_with("rollback users get release ") {
        if let Some((_,tail))=prefix.split_once(" quotas on ") && let Some(table)=table_prefix(tail,tables) {return table;}
        if let Some((_,tail))=prefix.split_once("'s ") && let Some(table)=table_prefix(tail,tables) {return table;}
    }
    if text.starts_with("release ") {
        if let Some(token)=prefix.split_whitespace().last() && let Some((owner,effect))=token.rsplit_once('.') {
            if effect=="require" {return format!("operation {owner}");}
            if tables.contains(owner) && matches!(effect,"read"|"insert"|"update"|"delete") {return owner.into();}
        }
        for name in programs.keys() {
            if prefix.ends_with(&format!(" operation {name}")) {return format!("operation {name}");}
        }
    }
    "release behavior".into()
}
fn brief(text: &str) -> String {
    // Semicolons also separate authored guards and multiple cap declarations;
    // retaining the full fact avoids dropping their contracts or caveats.
    text.to_owned()
}
pub(super) fn print(current: Option<&Schema>, target: &Schema, programs: &BTreeMap<String,Program>, warnings: &[String], notes: &[String], steps: &[Step], items: &[DormantItem]) {
    let tables: BTreeSet<_>=target.tables.keys().chain(current.into_iter().flat_map(|s|s.tables.keys())).cloned().collect();
    let mut groups=BTreeMap::<String,Group>::new();
    for (warning, lines) in [(true,warnings),(false,notes)] {
        for line in lines {
            let group=groups.entry(subject(line,&tables,programs)).or_default();
            let priority=if line.contains("safety guard") || line.contains(".require;") {0} else if line.contains("confidentiality") || line.contains("safety rule") {1} else {2};
            group.priority=group.priority.min(priority);
            let text=if priority==0 {line.clone()} else {brief(line)};
            let dest=if warning {&mut group.warnings} else {&mut group.notes};
            if !dest.contains(&text) {dest.push(text);}
        }
    }
    for step in steps {
        let path=step.path.strip_prefix("tables.").unwrap_or(&step.path);
        let key=table_prefix(path,&tables).unwrap_or_else(||path.to_owned());
        if path.strip_prefix(&key).is_some_and(|tail|tail.starts_with(".indexes.")) {continue;}
        let group=groups.entry(key).or_default();
        // Keep each user-visible source change even when another fact already
        // names this table. Only index plumbing is verbose-only.
        let detail=brief(&format!("{}: {}",path.replace(".columns.","."),step.message));
        if !group.notes.contains(&detail) {group.notes.push(detail);}
    }
    let mut storage=BTreeMap::<String,[u64;3]>::new();
    for item in items.iter().filter(|item|item.rows>0 && item.kind!="backfill") {
        let name=table_prefix(&item.path,&tables).unwrap_or_else(||item.path.clone());
        let slot=match item.kind.as_str() {"column"=>1,"index"=>2,_=>0};
        storage.entry(name).or_default()[slot]+=item.rows;
    }
    for (name,[rows,cells,indexes]) in storage {
        groups.entry(name).or_default().notes.push(format!("retained: {rows} dormant rows, {cells} cells, {indexes} index entries"));
    }
    for item in items.iter().filter(|item|item.kind=="backfill" && item.rows>0) {
        let name=table_prefix(&item.path,&tables).unwrap_or_else(||item.path.clone());
        groups.entry(name).or_default().notes.push(format!("retained: {} private backfill preimages ({} bytes)",item.rows,item.bytes));
    }
    let mut groups=groups.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();
    groups.sort_by_key(|(name,g)|(g.priority,name.clone()));
    for (name,mut group) in groups {
        let warning=!group.warnings.is_empty();
        group.warnings.append(&mut group.notes);
        println!("  {} {name}: {}{}",if warning {"WARNING"} else {"note:"},group.warnings.join("; "),if warning {"; verify these cases or preserve the current behavior in a bridge release"} else {""});
    }
}

#[test]
fn authored_values_cannot_assign_a_guard_to_an_unrelated_table() {

}

// A prior transformation's retained added output is not its own old argument
// on forward selection after rollback. Other declarations still see the new
// predecessor snapshot rather than an old cohort's overwritten columns.
fn inactive_snapshot(tx:&Tx<'_>,previous:Option<&Schema>,keys:&BTreeSet<String>)->Result<(),RuntimeError>{
    let mut q=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT t,id,definition FROM _backfill_evidence WHERE active=0 ORDER BY t,id,definition")?;
    let mut rows=q.query([])?;
    while let Some(r)=rows.next()? {
        let t:i64=r.get(0)?;let id:String=r.get(1)?;let key:String=r.get(2)?;if !keys.contains(&key){continue;}
        let name:String=tx.conn().query_row("SELECT name FROM _catalog WHERE num=?1",[t],|r|r.get(0))?;
        let old=previous.and_then(|s|s.table(&name));
        let e=evidence(tx,t,&id,&key)?.unwrap();
        let absent:Vec<_>=e.after.keys().filter(|c|!e.before.contains_key(*c) && old.is_none_or(|t|!t.columns.contains_key(*c))).cloned().collect();
        if absent.is_empty(){continue;}
        let data:Option<String>=tx.conn().query_row("SELECT data FROM r WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2",params![t,id],|r|r.get(0)).optional()?;let Some(data)=data else{continue};
        tx.conn().execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO temp._backfill_originals SELECT t,id,data FROM r WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2",params![t,id])?;
        let mut row:Value=decode(&data)?;if let Value::Row(fields)|Value::Map(fields)=&mut row {for c in absent {fields.insert(c,Value::Null);}}
        tx.conn().execute("UPDATE r SET data=?1 WHERE t=?2 AND id=?3",params![canonical_json(&row),t,id])?;
    }Ok(())
}

// Empty definition denotes currently omitted physical input cells; a definition
// digest denotes absence at that receipt's adoption. Defaults may materialize
// during retention without turning omitted inputs into authored values.
pub(super) fn prepare_inputs(tx:&Tx<'_>,next:&Schema,previous:Option<&Schema>)->Result<(),RuntimeError>{
    if next.backfills.is_empty() && previous.is_none_or(|s|s.backfills.is_empty()) && !present(tx)? {return Ok(());}
    enable(tx)?;
    tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _backfill_active",[])?;
    for fill in &next.backfills {tx.conn().execute("INSERT INTO _backfill_active VALUES(?1,?2,?3)",params![tx.num(&fill.table)?,fill.key(),canonical_json(&fill.inputs.keys().collect::<Vec<_>>())])?;}
    for fill in next.backfills.iter().chain(previous.into_iter().flat_map(|s|s.backfills.iter())) {
        tx.conn().execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO _backfill_definitions VALUES(?1,?2)",params![fill.key(),canonical_json(fill)])?;
        for c in fill.inputs.keys() {tx.conn().execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO _backfill_inputs VALUES(?1,?2)",params![tx.num(&fill.table)?,c])?;}
    }
    let tables:Vec<i64>=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT DISTINCT t FROM _backfill_inputs")?.query_map([],|r|r.get(0))?.collect::<Result<_,_>>()?;
    for t in tables {
        let columns:Vec<String>=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT column_name FROM _backfill_inputs WHERE t=?1")?.query_map([t],|r|r.get(0))?.collect::<Result<_,_>>()?;
        super::activation::walk(tx,t,|id,row|{
            for c in &columns {if row.field(c).is_err(){note_omission(tx,t,id,c)?;}}
            Ok(())
        })?;
    } Ok(())
}
pub(super) fn observe_write(tx:&Tx<'_>,t:i64,id:&str,table:&Table,row:&Value,old:Option<&Value>)->Result<(),RuntimeError>{
    if !present(tx)? {return Ok(());}
    if old.is_none() {
        let active:Vec<(String,String)>=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT definition,input_names FROM _backfill_active WHERE t=?1")?.query_map([t],|r|Ok((r.get(0)?,r.get(1)?)))?.collect::<Result<_,_>>()?;
        for (key,names) in active {
            let names:Vec<String>=decode(&names)?;let absent=names.iter().filter(|c|row.field(c).is_err()).cloned().collect();
            let fingerprint=input_fingerprint(row,names.iter().map(String::as_str),&absent);
            tx.conn().execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO _backfill_absence VALUES(?1,?2,?3,?4)",params![t,id,format!("$native:{key}"),fingerprint])?;
        }
    }
    let columns:Vec<String>=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT column_name FROM _backfill_inputs WHERE t=?1")?.query_map([t],|r|r.get(0))?.collect::<Result<_,_>>()?;
    if columns.is_empty(){return Ok(());}
    let interpreted_old=old.map(|r|crate::schema::row_image(r,table));
    let interpreted_new=crate::schema::row_image(row,table);
    for c in columns {
        let changed=interpreted_old.as_ref().is_none_or(|before|before.field(&c).ok()!=interpreted_new.field(&c).ok());
        if changed {tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _backfill_absence WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2 AND column_name=?3",params![t,id,c])?;}
        }
        let (chunk, logs) = engine_work(shared, |engine, budget| (engine.run_job_chunk_for(shared.now(), budget), engine.take_native_logs()));
        for line in logs { snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: native {line}"); }
        match chunk {
            Ok(Some(chunk)) if chunk.state == JobState::Parked && shared.personas => shared.refusals.job(&chunk),
            Ok(_) => {}
            Err(error) => return respond(request, 500, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error.refusal())})),
        }
    };
    snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: job {} {} on request: {} chunk{}, {} row{} written", run.name, if run.state == JobState::Done { "done" } else { "parked" },
        run.chunks, if run.chunks == 1 { "" } else { "s" }, run.rows_written, if run.rows_written == 1 { "" } else { "s" });
    respond(request, 200, json!({ "job": run.name, "id": run.id, "state": run.state, "chunks": run.chunks, "chunkSize": run.chunk_size, "retries": run.retries, "heapPeak": run.heap_peak, "rowsWritten": run.rows_written, "error": run.error }));
}

pub(super) fn clock_status(request: Request, shared: &Shared) {
    if let Err(why) = clock_service(&request, shared) { return respond(request,403,json!({"denied":refusal_json(&why)})); }
    let result = (|| {
        let (epoch, reader) = shared.reader()?;
        let note = crate::dev_clock_store::ahead(&reader, shared.now());
        lock(&shared.readers).put(&epoch, reader.into_inner());
        note
    })();
    match result {
        Ok(note) => { let now = shared.now(); respond(request, 200, json!({"storeAhead":note,"now":now,"skewMs":now - snapback4_core::now_ms()})) },
        Err(error) => respond(request, 500, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error.refusal())})),
    }
}

    45	        tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key = 'time_audience_clock'", [])?;

    64	        // and the next crossed boundary fires normally. Replay's count restarts.

pub(crate) fn seed_rows(schema: &Schema, tx: &crate::store::Tx<'_>, rows: impl IntoIterator<Item = (String, Value)>, now: i64) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
    let bounded=crate::schema::live::has_live(schema);
    let mut bulk_meter=Meter::new(if bounded {Ceilings::job()}else{Ceilings::unbounded()},Cut::Abort);
    let rows:Box<dyn Iterator<Item=(String,Value)> + '_>=if bounded {Box::new(live_bulk::collect(rows,&mut bulk_meter)?.into_iter())}else{Box::new(rows.into_iter())};
    let rows = through_activation::ancestor_order(schema, rows);
    let targets: std::collections::BTreeSet<_> = schema.tables.values().flat_map(|table| table.recorded.values().map(|field| field.table.as_str())).collect();
    let mut imports = BTreeMap::<(String, String), Value>::new();
    let rows: Box<dyn Iterator<Item = (String, Value)> + '_> = if targets.is_empty() { Box::new(rows.into_iter()) } else {
        let rows: Vec<_> = rows.into_iter().collect();
        // A capture sees the imported target's eventual image, including
        // fields retained by patches, defaults and assigned ordinals.
        // Preview every allocation in input order (counters cross tables),
        // then undo the preview; ordinary writes allocate in that same
        // transaction and still own all validation, events and rollback.
        tx.savepoint("seed_sequences")?;
        let mut staging = Runner::new(tx, schema, Context::system().at(now), bulk_meter, 0);
        for (name, row) in &rows {
            if bounded {staging.reserve_bulk_source(name)?;staging.meter.heap(crate::rows::disclosed::decode_reservation(&schema.tables[name]).saturating_mul(4))?;}
            schema.refuse_ephemeral_import(name)?;
            let table = schema.table(name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {name}")))?;
            sequences::refuse_fields(table, name, row)?;
            let id = row.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
            let old = match imports.get(&(name.clone(), id.clone())) { Some(row) => Some(row.clone()), None => tx.get(name, &id)? }.filter(|row| !table.expired(row, now));
            let mut fields = old.as_ref().map(|row| row.as_object().cloned()).transpose()?.unwrap_or_default();
            fields.extend(row.as_object()?.clone());
            if old.is_none() { for (field, default) in &table.defaults { fields.entry(field.clone()).or_insert_with(|| default.value(now, crate::SYSTEM_PRINCIPAL)); } }
            let mut image = Value::Row(fields.into());
            if old.is_none() {
                let (assigned, full) = staging.sequence_fields(name, image.import_input(&ImportInput(())))?;
                if full { return Err(sequences::exhausted()); }
                staging.commit_sequences(name, &assigned)?;
                image = assigned;
            }
            imports.insert((name.clone(), id), image);
        }
        bulk_meter=staging.meter.clone();
        drop(staging);
        tx.rollback_to("seed_sequences")?;
        Box::new(rows.into_iter())
    };
        by.iter().any(|column| self.on_delete.get(column) == Some(&references::OnDelete::SetNull))
    }

    pub fn immutable_fields(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {
        self.constraints.iter().flat_map(|constraint| match constraint {
            Constraint::Immutable { fields } => fields.iter().map(String::as_str).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            _ => Vec::new(),
        })
    }

    /// Whether `row` is past its `expire` column at `now`: absent to every
    /// reader, pending the sweep. A null time never expires.
    pub fn expired(&self, row: &Value, now: i64) -> bool {
        self.deadline(row).is_some_and(|at| at <= now)
    }

    /// The index the expiry sweep walks: the first leading with the
    /// `expire` column, as the declaration requires.
    pub fn expiry_index(&self) -> Option<(&str, &Index)> {
        let column = self.expiry_column()?;
        self.indexes.iter().find(|(_, index)| {
                index.is_plain() && index.columns().first().map(String::as_str) == Some(column)
            }).map(|(name, index)| (name.as_str(), index))
    }

    /// The column carrying the principal a `sync to T[...]` audience reads.
    pub fn principal_columns(&self) -> Vec<&str> {
        self.columns.iter().filter(|(_, kind)| matches!(kind, ColumnType::Principal)).map(|(name, _)| name.as_str()).collect()
    }
}


fn is_false(value: &bool) -> bool {
    !*value
}

impl fmt::Display for ColumnType {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Self::Id => f.write_str("id"),
            Self::Principal => f.write_str("principal"),
            Self::Text { max } => write!(f, "text <={max}"),
            Self::Bytes { max } => write!(f, "bytes <={max}"),
            Self::Image { max, once: false } => write!(f, "image <={max}"),
            Self::Image { max, once: true } => write!(f, "image <={max} once"),
            Self::Video { max } => write!(f, "video <={max}"),
            Self::File { max, types } if types.is_empty() => write!(f, "file <={max}"),
            Self::File { max, types } => write!(f, "file <={max} ({})", types.iter().map(|t| format!("'{t}'")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")),
            Self::Int => f.write_str("int"),
            Self::IntRange { min, max } => f.write_str(&int_range_text(int_bound(*min, int_floor()), int_bound(*max, int_ceiling()))),
            Self::Enum { variants } => write!(f, "enum({})", variants.iter().map(|v| format!("'{v}'")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")),
            Self::Decimal { scale } => write!(f, "decimal {scale}"),
            Self::Money { currency, scale } => write!(f, "money {currency} {scale}"),
            Self::Bool => f.write_str("bool"),
            Self::Time => f.write_str("time"),
            Self::Ref { table } => f.write_str(table),
            Self::Json { max_bytes } => write!(f, "json <={max_bytes}"),
            Self::Optional(inner) => write!(f, "{inner} ?"),
            Self::List { of, max } => write!(f, "[{of}] <={max}"),
            Self::ListRange { of, min, max } => write!(f, "[{of}] {min}..{max}"),
        }
    }
}

/// `int M..N`, `int M..` or `int ..N`, the one spelling of each bound.
pub fn int_range_text(min: Option<i64>, max: Option<i64>) -> String {
    match (min, max) {
        (Some(min), Some(max)) => format!("int {min}..{max}"),
        (Some(min), None) => format!("int {min}.."),
        (None, Some(max)) => format!("int ..{max}"),
        (None, None) => "int".into(),
    }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.040#13-representation — an unwritten end is the i53 limit itself, so the
// variant stays as small as `Int`'s neighbours (no Option) and the bytes omit it.
pub fn int_floor() -> i64 { -crate::value::I53_MAX }
pub fn int_ceiling() -> i64 { crate::value::I53_MAX }
pub fn is_int_floor(min: &i64) -> bool { *min <= int_floor() }
pub fn is_int_ceiling(max: &i64) -> bool { *max >= int_ceiling() }
/// An int range some i53 value satisfies, with both ends inside i53.
pub fn int_range_valid(min: i64, max: i64) -> bool { int_floor() <= min && min <= max && max <= int_ceiling() }
/// A stored end as written: `None` when it is the i53 limit.
pub fn int_bound(end: i64, limit: i64) -> Option<i64> { (end != limit).then_some(end) }

/// Whether `value` lies inside an inclusive optional range.
pub fn int_in_range(value: i64, min: Option<i64>, max: Option<i64>) -> bool {
    min.is_none_or(|min| value >= min) && max.is_none_or(|max| value <= max)
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Index {
    pub components: Vec<IndexComponent>,
    pub unique: bool,
}

impl Index {
    pub fn of(columns: &[&str], unique: bool) -> Self {
        Self { components: columns.iter().map(|c| IndexComponent::Column((*c).to_owned())).collect(), unique }
    }

    /// Ordered key names: columns and time-function names. A `words(..)`
    /// component contributes nothing here; `word_component` names it.
    /// Use `IndexComponent::column` for actual row fields (such as rule pins).
    pub fn columns(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        self.components.iter().filter_map(|c| c.key_name().cloned()).collect()
    }

    pub fn is_plain(&self) -> bool {
        self.components.iter().all(|c| matches!(c, IndexComponent::Column(_)))
    }

    pub fn uses_column(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.components.iter().any(|component| match component {
            IndexComponent::Column(column) => column == name,
            IndexComponent::Calendar(key) => key.column == name,
            IndexComponent::WordPrefixes { fields, .. } => fields.iter().any(|field| field == name),
            IndexComponent::Contribution(maintain) => maintain.dependencies().contains(name),
        })
    };
    let seq = tx.next_seq()?;
    let mut runner = Runner::new(tx, schema, Context::system().at(now), bulk_meter, seq);
    runner.import_targets = Some(&imports);
    let mut count = 0;
    for (table, row) in rows {
        if bounded {runner.reserve_bulk_source(&table)?;}
        schema.refuse_ephemeral_import(&table)?;
        timeline::check_import(schema, &table)?;
        runner.upsert(&table, &row.field("id")?.clone(), row.import_input(&ImportInput(())))?;
        count += 1;
    }
    // Seeds preserve ordinary expired images for a later sweep. A source of
    // a row-keyed view is the established exception: an already-expired
    // seeded image must not enter a committed count basis or revive after
    // a clock rollback. Route only those sources through the common retirement
    // path so reference actions and net maintenance still run transactionally.
    // @ref LLP 3000.039#6.5 — seeded expired row-view sources retire with actions; unrelated expired fixtures remain stored.
    let final_exists = runner.satisfied_final_exists()?;
    runner.retire_seeded_view_sources()?;
    // Seeds historically admit fixture rows whose obligations are not
    // meaningful under the system viewer. Retirement may not invalidate an
    // obligation that did hold immediately before its reference actions.
    runner.check_final_exists_witnesses(&final_exists)?;
    let events = runner.events.take();
    let tables: Vec<String> = runner.written_tables.iter().cloned().collect();
    drop(runner);
    if count > 0 {
        tx.record_commit(seq, now, "seed", crate::SYSTEM_PRINCIPAL, "seed", &tables, count)?;
        partition::append(tx, seq, &events)?;
    }
    Ok(count)
    }

// @ref LLP 3000.036.002#8 — durable and ephemeral seats receive the same static clause for every private cause.
#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
pub fn seat_refusal(schema:&Schema,error:&RuntimeError,viewer:&str)->Refusal {
    let mut why=error.refusal();
    if viewer.starts_with("service:") && let RuntimeError::Rule {table,effect}|RuntimeError::AuthorizationBudget {table,effect}=error {
        if let Some(def)=schema.table(table) {why.message.push_str(&format!("; {table} rule clause: {effect} <- {}",def.rules.for_effect(*effect).quarry()));}
    }
    why
}

impl Store {
    /// Inspect a dev store without creating a database, changing permissions, or
    /// running the writable store's initialization and upgrade path.
    pub fn open_read_only(path: &Path) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
        let mut conn = Connection::open_with_flags(path, rusqlite::OpenFlags::SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY)?;
        #[cfg(unix)]
        let file_identity = file_identity(&conn)?;
        conn.busy_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))?;
        let tx = conn.transaction()?;
        let version: String = tx.query_row("SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key = 'version'", [], |row| {
                row.get(0)
            })?;
        if version != STORE_VERSION && version != dormant::VERSION && version != "snapback4-release-store-2" && version != backfills::VERSION { return Err(RuntimeError::Store(format!("store version {version} is not {STORE_VERSION}"))); }
        let catalog = tx.prepare("SELECT name, num FROM _catalog")?.query_map([], |row| Ok((row.get(0)?, row.get(1)?)))?.collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
        let identity = activation::identity(&tx)?;
        tx.rollback()?;
        let real = std::fs::canonicalize(path).unwrap_or_else(|_| path.to_path_buf());
        let assets_dir = real.parent().unwrap_or(Path::new(".")).join("assets");
        let page_size = conn.query_row("PRAGMA page_size", [], |row| row.get::<_, i64>(0))? as u64;
        Ok(Self { #[cfg(test)] full_adoption: false, adoption_report: Default::default(), conn,
            server: false, ownership: None, #[cfg(unix)] file_identity, page_size, catalog, identity, assets_dir, ephemeral_assets: false })
    }

    /// Classify against one read snapshot of the active generation and rows.
    pub fn successor(&mut self, schema: &Schema) -> Result<Vec<crate::successor::Step>, RuntimeError> {
        let tx = self.read_transaction()?;
        let steps = successor::assess(&tx, schema)?;
        tx.rollback()?;
        Ok(steps)
    }

    /// Preview the same atomic launch admitted by dev, without changing the store.
    pub fn check_timeline_activation(&mut self, schema: &Schema) -> Result<Vec<timeline_launch::Estimate>, RuntimeError> {
        self.check_timeline_activation_at(schema, crate::now_ms(), true)
    }

    pub fn check_timeline_activation_at(&mut self, schema: &Schema, now: i64, allow_launch: bool) -> Result<Vec<timeline_launch::Estimate>, RuntimeError> {
        let tx = self.read_transaction()?;
        let estimates = timeline_launch::preflight(&tx, schema, now, allow_launch)?;
        tx.rollback()?;
        Ok(estimates)
    }

    pub fn open(path: &Path) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
        Self::open_with_busy_timeout(path, std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))
    }

//! Privileged, bounded population evidence for adoption refusals.
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#3-older-writes-and-incompatible-values — count all affected rows, retain at most five samples.
use super::*;
use crate::schema::{Constraint, materialize_optional_fields};

#[derive(Default)]
pub(super) struct Samples {
    pub count: u64,
    ids: Vec<String>,
    values: Vec<String>,
    last_id: Option<String>,
}
pub(super) fn bounded(text: &str) -> String {
    if text.len() <= 256 {
        return text.into();
    }
    let mut end = 256;
    while !text.is_char_boundary(end) {
        end -= 1;
    }
    format!("{}… [truncated]", &text[..end])
}

fn value_sample(value: &Value) -> String {
    struct Prefix(Vec<u8>);
    impl std::io::Write for Prefix {
        fn write(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<usize> {
            let n = bytes.len().min(256 - self.0.len());
            self.0.extend_from_slice(&bytes[..n]);
            if n < bytes.len() {
                return Err(std::io::Error::other("sample truncated"));
            }
            Ok(n)
        }
        fn flush(&mut self) -> std::io::Result<()> {
            Ok(())
        }
    }
    if let Value::Bytes(bytes) = value {
        return format!("{} bytes", bytes.len());
    }
    let mut prefix = Prefix(Vec::with_capacity(256));
    let truncated = serde_json::to_writer(&mut prefix, &crate::wire::Plain(value)).is_err();
    let mut text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&prefix.0).into_owned();
    if truncated {
        text.push_str("… [truncated]")
    }
    text
}
impl Samples {
    pub fn add(&mut self, id: &str, value: &str) {
        if self.last_id.as_deref() != Some(id) {
            self.count += 1;
            if self.ids.len() < 5 {
                self.ids.push(bounded(id));
            }
            self.last_id = Some(id.into());
        }
        let value = bounded(value);
        if self.values.len() < 5 && !self.values.contains(&value) {
            self.values.push(value);
        }
    }
    pub fn describe(&self) -> String {
        format!(
            "{} affected rows; sample ids [{}]; values/keys [{}]",
            self.count,
            self.ids.join(", "),
            self.values.join(", ")
        )
    }
}

pub(super) fn candidate(
    tx: &Tx<'_>,
    schema: &Schema,
    previous: Option<&Schema>,
    complete: bool,
) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    for (name, table) in schema
        .tables
        .iter()
        .filter(|(n, t)| t.ephemeral.is_none() && schema.maintain_for(n).is_none())
    {
        if previous.and_then(|p| p.table(name)) == Some(table) {
            continue;
        }
        let mut bad = Samples::default();
        super::activation::walk(tx, tx.num(name)?, |id, mut row| {
            if let Value::Row(f) | Value::Map(f) = &mut row {
                f.retain(|c, _| table.columns.contains_key(c));
            }
            materialize_optional_fields(&mut row, table);
            let validation = if complete {
                crate::engine::validate::validate_row(schema, name, &row)
            } else {

//! Deadline ownership follows read emission, independently of the work meter.
use std::{cell::Cell, rc::Rc};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]
struct Frame {
    deadline: Option<i64>,
    depth: u32,
}

/// A detached prefix decision may seed candidates, but cannot publish a deadline.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]
pub(super) struct Pending(Option<i64>);

/// One fixed control cell per runner. Marks are stack-sized handles; nesting
/// allocates no row-dependent storage and follows the interpreter's bounded stack.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct Expiry(Rc<Cell<Frame>>);

// @ref LLP 3000.014#5-what-derives-from-the-capture — authorization and recount deadlines are provisional until their answer is emitted.
impl Expiry {
    pub(crate) fn get(&self) -> Option<i64> {
        debug_assert_eq!(
            self.0.get().depth,
            0,
            "reply has an unfinished expiry scope"
        );
        self.0.get().deadline
    }

    pub(super) fn scope(&self) -> Mark {
        let parent = self.0.replace(Frame {
            deadline: None,
            depth: self.0.get().depth + 1,
        });
        Mark {
            cell: self.0.clone(),
            parent,
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn note(&self, at: i64) {
        let mut frame = self.0.get();
        // Raw authorization outside a read (for example a write check) has
        // no emitted answer to own a deadline.
        if frame.depth == 0 {
            return;
        }
        frame.deadline = Some(frame.deadline.map_or(at, |prior| prior.min(at)));
        self.0.set(frame);
    }

    pub(super) fn inherit(&self, pending: Pending) {
        if let Some(at) = pending.0 {
            self.note(at);
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn note_option(&self, at: Option<i64>) {
        if let Some(at) = at {
            self.note(at);
        }
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000.015#2 — the complete-rule evaluator isolates each witness
    // leaf's deadline and restores the frame with the whole rule's boundary.
    // Outside an emitting read the frame is detached: a raw write check owns
    // no deadline and observes none, exactly as `note` above.
    pub(super) fn replace(&self, deadline: Option<i64>) -> Option<i64> {
        let mut frame = self.0.get();
        if frame.depth == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        let prior = frame.deadline;
        frame.deadline = deadline;
        self.0.set(frame);
        prior
    }
}

impl Pending {
//! Explicit recovery for physically missing expiry parents; absence has no provenance.
// @ref LLP 3000.039#13-wave-13-expiry-orphan-recovery — inspect without writes; only an operator-selected missing identity can trigger recovery.
use super::{Engine, Runner, time_audience};
use crate::{Context, Value, error::RuntimeError, meter::{Ceilings, Cut, Meter}, schema::{BY_ID, Schema}, store::{Bounds, Dir}};
use std::collections::BTreeSet;

fn eligible(schema: &Schema, parent: &str) -> bool {
    schema.actionable(parent) && schema.table(parent).is_some_and(|table| table.expire.is_some())
        && schema.referencing(parent).iter().any(|reference| reference.action.writes())
}

impl Engine {
    /// At most `limit` missing parent identities, in schema/row order. A single
    /// coherent read snapshot, bounded row pages, no adoption or repair writes.
    /// These can also be deliberately dangling references, never proven expiry.
    pub fn expiry_orphans(&mut self, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<(String, String)>, RuntimeError> {
        let tx = self.store.read_transaction()?;
        let mut found = BTreeSet::new();
        if limit == 0 { return Ok(Vec::new()); }
        for parent in self.schema.tables.keys().filter(|parent| eligible(&self.schema, parent)) {
            for reference in self.schema.referencing(parent).iter().filter(|reference| reference.action.writes()) {
                let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
                loop {
                    let page = tx.scan(reference.child, BY_ID, &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 128)?;
                    let count = page.len();
                    for (row, key) in page {
                        bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
                        let value = row.field(reference.column)?;
                        if value == &Value::Null { continue; }
                        let id = value.as_str()?;
                        if tx.get(parent, id)?.is_none() {
                            found.insert((parent.clone(), id.to_owned()));
                            if found.len() >= limit { return Ok(found.into_iter().collect()); }
                        }
                    }
                    if count < 128 { break; }
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(found.into_iter().collect())
    }

    /// The host has selected this missing root explicitly. Apply the current
    /// schema's ordinary bounded reference closure; never fabricate a parent
    /// image or restore it, bypass a blocker, or commit partial child actions.
    pub fn repair_expiry_orphan(&mut self, parent: &str, id: &str, now: i64) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        if id.is_empty() || !eligible(&self.schema, parent) {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Schema("expiry orphan recovery needs an expiring parent table with cascade or set-null references and a nonempty id".into()));
        }
        let tx = self.store.transaction()?;
        if tx.get(parent, id)?.is_some() {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Schema("expiry orphan recovery requires a physically missing parent; an existing expired parent uses the ordinary sweep".into()));
        }
        let now = time_audience::pin_writer_time(&self.schema, &tx, now)?;
        let seq = tx.next_seq()?;
        let mut runner = Runner::new(&tx, &self.schema, Context::system().at(now), Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort), seq);
        let identity = crate::value::object([("id", Value::Id(id.into()))]);
        runner.apply_missing_reference_actions(parent, &identity)?;
        let events = runner.events.take();
        let tables = runner.written_tables.iter().cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let written = runner.rows_written;
        drop(runner);
        if written > 0 {
            tx.record_commit(seq, now, "repair expiry orphan", crate::SYSTEM_PRINCIPAL, &format!("{parent}:{id}"), &tables, written)?;
            super::partition::append(&tx, seq, &events)?;
        }
        tx.commit()?;
        Ok(written)
    }
}

//! Referential actions on delete (LLP 3000.039 §3): before a delete removes
//! its row, reserve a schema-fixed charge, close over the `cascade`
//! references, refuse while a `restrict` reference still holds a closure row
//! from outside the closure, clear `set null` references outside it, and
//! remove the closure children first. The caller then removes the row itself.
// @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — closure first; probes exclude the closure; deletion dominates set null.
use crate::engine::runner::Runner;
use crate::{
    error::{MeterKind, RuntimeError},
    meter::{Ceilings, Cut, Meter},
    rows::{Bounds, Dir},
    schema::{Effect, references::{OnDelete, Referencing}},
    value::Value,
};
use std::collections::BTreeSet;

impl Runner<'_> {
    pub(super) fn apply_reference_actions(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: &Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.reference_actions(table_name, old, false)
    }

    // Recovery has no later root-delete hook to preflight physical read-through
    // retention. Include that root before the first child action can write.
    pub(in crate::engine) fn apply_missing_reference_actions(&mut self, table_name: &str, identity: &Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.reference_actions(table_name, identity, true)
    }

    fn reference_actions(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: &Value, missing_root: bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let schema = self.schema;
        if !schema.is_referenced(table_name) { return Ok(()); }
        let Some(price) = schema.delete_reservation(table_name) else {
            // A device without a reached child's exported price cannot charge
            // what the server charges; the server always has every price.
            if self.device { return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(format!("deleting {table_name} needs every referencing table's write price; queued without a local delete"))); }
            return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{table_name}'s delete actions have no reservation: a cascading reference lacks its cap or its child's write price (guide writes)")));
        };
        // @ref LLP 3000.039#4.2 — what the commit publishes is fixed by the schema, not by the rows the actions reach.
        let closure = schema.action_tables(table_name);
        // A public device projection carries the private column's price but
        // not the maintain that computes its value. If an action can write
        // such a source, settlement must supply the authoritative mirror.
        // @ref LLP 3000.007.001#3.7 — devices store maintained columns but never derive them.
        if self.device && closure.written.iter().any(|source| schema.write_reservation(source)
            .is_some_and(|plan| plan.price(crate::schema::reservations::COLUMNS)[3] != 0)) {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(format!("deleting {table_name} can change a server-maintained column; queued without a local delete")));
        }
        for table in &closure.written {
            if schema.visible(table) { self.written_tables.insert(table.clone()); }
            self.action_tables.insert(table.clone());
        }
        for table in &closure.read { self.read_tables.insert(table.clone()); }
        if !closure.written.is_empty() { self.tx.widen_change_evidence(); }
        for (kind, amount) in [(MeterKind::Steps, price[0]), (MeterKind::IndexEntries, price[1]), (MeterKind::Examined, price[2]), (MeterKind::RowsWritten, price[3]), (MeterKind::OutputBytes, price[5]), (MeterKind::RuleProbes, price[6])] {
            if amount > 0 { self.meter.charge(kind, amount)?; }
        }
        // Pending event images survive the closure and subsequent statements.
        // Keep their schema-fixed reservation until the request ends.
        let events = schema.delete_event_heap(table_name).unwrap_or(0);
        self.meter.heap(events)?;
        let mark = self.meter.mark();
        self.meter.heap(price[4].saturating_sub(events))?;
        // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — draw the reservation's rows from the request's physical allowance before the first seek.
        if !self.context.is_system() { self.tx.draw(table_name, price[2])?; }
        let meter = std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter, Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort));
        // The fixed action reservation prepays the closure itself, but held-
        // group and authority proofs remain device-only bounded work. Keep the
        // active allowance reachable by nested `device_work` calls while the
        // closure runs under its prepaid unbounded meter. Recursive cascade
        // removals see the already-stored allowance and must not take it over.
        // @ref LLP 3000.039#6.4 — every device-only proof spends the separate bounded physical-work allowance.
        let owns_device_allowance = self.device_work_active && self.device_allowance.is_none();
        let mut meter = Some(meter);
        if owns_device_allowance { self.device_allowance = meter.take(); }
        let prepaid = self.tx.reference_prepaid(true);
        let action = std::mem::replace(&mut self.engine_action, true);
        let result = self.reference_closure(table_name, old, missing_root);
        self.engine_action = action;
        self.tx.reference_prepaid(prepaid);
        self.meter = if owns_device_allowance {
            self.device_allowance.take().expect("active device allowance")
        } else {
            meter.expect("prepaid action meter")
        };
        self.meter.release_heap(mark);
        result
    }

    /// Steps 3–6. The walk holds identities, never images: each child scan
    /// streams `PAGE` rows per seek, and every write rereads its row current.
    fn reference_closure(&mut self, root_table: &str, root: &Value, missing_root: bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let schema = self.schema;
        let mut seen: BTreeSet<(String, String)> = BTreeSet::from([(root_table.to_owned(), root.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned())]);
        // (Vectors, not maps: the web device pays for every new collection type.)
        let mut visits: Vec<(String, Value)> = vec![(root_table.to_owned(), root.field("id")?.clone())];
        // 3. Close over cascades, breadth first. Every reached row's referencing groups must be held on a device.
        let mut next = 0;
        while next < visits.len() {
            let (table, id) = visits[next].clone();
            next += 1;
            for r in schema.referencing(&table) {
                if self.device && !through_reference(&r) { self.prove_reference_held(&r, &id)?; }
                if r.action != OnDelete::Cascade { continue; }
                self.each_child(&r, &id, true, &mut |_, child| {
                    if seen.insert((r.child.to_owned(), child.as_str()?.to_owned())) { visits.push((r.child.to_owned(), child)); }
                    Ok(true)
                })?;
            }
        }
        // 4. Restrict: every probe runs, streaming past closure rows (the root
        // included) to the first outside witness; the first occupied reference
        // in schema order is reported. One reference's probes visit each closure
        // row at most once, plus one witness per probe (LLP 3000.039 §5.1).
        let mut occupied: Option<(String, String, String)> = None;
        for (table, id) in &visits {
            for r in schema.referencing(table) {
                if r.action != OnDelete::Restrict || through_reference(&r) { continue; }
                let mut outside = false;
                self.each_child(&r, id, false, &mut |_, child| {
                    outside = !seen.contains(&(r.child.to_owned(), child.as_str()?.to_owned()));
                    Ok(!outside)
                })?;
                let candidate = (r.child.to_owned(), r.column.to_owned(), table.clone());
                if outside && occupied.as_ref().is_none_or(|o| candidate < *o) { occupied = Some(candidate); }
            }
        }
        if let Some((child, column, parent)) = occupied {
            #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
            self.refusing_clause(&child, &format!("{column}: {parent} (on delete restrict)"));
            let via = if parent == root_table { String::new() } else { format!(", through a {parent} row this delete cascades to") };
            return Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_REFERENCED", message: format!("{root_table} at {} is still referenced through {child}.{column} (on delete restrict){via}; delete or retarget those rows first, or declare the reference's action (guide writes)", self.statement_site) });
        }
        // A cascaded row can itself have a physically retained read-through
        // child. Decide that blocker before set-null writes begin, so expiry
        // can retain this root and continue without relying on transaction
        // rollback to undo a partial closure.
        for (table, id) in visits.iter().skip(if missing_root { 0 } else { 1 }) {
            if self.physical_children_outside(table, id, &seen)? {
                return Err(self.parent_has_children(table));
            }
        }
        // 5. Set null outside the closure. Each group is gathered whole before
        // any of it is cleared: a clear can recount a sibling that shares the
        // reference's index and move it behind a page cursor. Each row is then
        // reread current before its write.
        // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — gather, then clear: no row moves out of a walk it has not finished.
        for (table, id) in &visits {
            for r in schema.referencing(table) {
                if r.action != OnDelete::SetNull { continue; }
                let mut group: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
                self.each_child(&r, id, true, &mut |_, child| {

    /// Physically retire one row whose upper lifetime ended. Expiry bypasses
    /// the root's authored delete rule and constraints, but it does not bypass
    /// the schema's declared effects on rows that reference the root. A
    /// read-through child still retains the expired parent physically.
    // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — expiry cleanup runs the same closure/restrict/set-null actions as an authored delete.
    pub(super) fn retire_expired_row(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: &Value) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
        if self.physical_children(table_name, old.field("id")?)? { return Ok(false); }
        let current = if self.schema.is_referenced(table_name) {
            self.apply_reference_actions(table_name, old)?;
            // A cascade may maintain a column on the root; delete its current
            // physical image so index and cap entries match what is stored.
            let id = old.field("id")?.as_str()?;
            self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, table_name, id))?
                .unwrap_or_else(|| old.clone())
        } else {
            old.clone()
        };
        self.remove(table_name, &current)?;
        Ok(true)
    }

    /// physical, so the log carries the deletion to each device holding
    /// them. At most `limit` rows go in one commit; the next pass continues.
    pub fn sweep_expired(&mut self, now: i64, limit: usize) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        self.sweep_expired_for(now, limit, std::time::Duration::MAX)
    }

    /// Stop between row removals; a short sweep can still leave due rows.
    pub fn sweep_expired_for(&mut self, now: i64, limit: usize, budget: std::time::Duration) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        // Expiry cleanup is recovery work. Pin the same authoritative clock,
        // but commit physical cleanup before attempting a due opening so a

- **P1 — Backfill retirement bypasses reference actions.** [narrowed.rs:256](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-b17-mig/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/store/narrowed.rs:256) physically deletes expired source rows through `Tx::delete`, bypassing ordinary expiry’s cascade, set-null, restrict, and retained-child checks. An unswept expired parent with cascade children can therefore disappear during an unrelated backfill while its children remain active; later sweeps cannot recover the missing parent’s deletion provenance. The restored-table path does the same at [dormant.rs:494](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-b17-mig/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/store/dormant.rs:494). Run the existing expiry/reference closure against the assembled source before evaluating patches, with atomic refusal for blockers.

- **P2 — Reset disables native-birth tracking.** [dev_reset.rs:60](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-b17-mig/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/dev_reset.rs:60) empties `_backfill_active` and `_backfill_inputs`, while retaining the adopted schema. Subsequent inserts receive no native marker because [backfills.rs:362](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-b17-mig/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/store/backfills.rs:362) relies on that registry. After resetting a schema with `derived = n * 2`, inserting `(n:3, derived:9)`, then rolling back and forward, the authored `9` is overwritten with `6`. Reinitialize declaration metadata from the retained schema before reset reseeding or subsequent writes.
